Its current thread had no message for the folder's idle minutes.
The caller asked for a new thread (`new: true`).

CurvePoint.description: One point of the threshold curve: what a cut at `threshold` keeps.

correct.description: Of those, the ones answered correctly.

covered.description: Answered items at or above it.

threshold.description: A confidence (certainty for `noul`) some answer has.

DecideAnswer.description:
The probe's `choice` answer, with the options in the order the model
gave them. A JSON object would lose that order on the way through an op
(the op's JSON is a sorted map), so the options are a list.

confidence.description: How certain the model is, derived from the probabilities.

probabilities.description:
Every option with its probability, in the order llama.cpp answered
them; they sum to 1.

DecisionBackend.description: Where a local decision row computes.

DecisionEstimate.description: One limit with the form's estimate against it.

over.description: The estimate is past the limit. A warning: Ask is not blocked.

tokens.description: The state plus the largest question, or the largest option span.

DecisionFacts.description:
A local decision row's facts: its row, its GGUF header and its running
server.

header_error.description:
Why the header could not be read; the header's fields are `null`
then.

max_head_tokens.description:
The header's `decision.max_head_tokens`: past it llama.cpp truncates a
question and its options.

n_ctx_slot.description:
One slot's context as the running server's `/props` says; `null`
until a container has run.

threads_in_effect.description:
The thread count its container runs with; `null` when llama-server
picks.

ubatch.description:
The ubatch in effect: the row's, its args', llama.cpp's default, never
above the batch.

DecisionFallbackPrice.description:
The price of the alias that answers for a held local row: `alias` and
what `DecisionPrice` says of a model, for its own primary route.

rows.description: The rows that price it, per unit, as `DecisionPrice::rows`.

unresolved.description: Why its route did not resolve; `rows` is empty then.

DecisionForm.description:
The Decision lab's whole form, as the page holds it and the store keeps
it (`lab_groups.form`). Every list is a `Vec`, so storing it keeps its
order.

state.description: As typed; JSON mode keeps its text verbatim.

oneOf.description: A new image, as the page read it.

An image the store keeps already (a re-opened form): its artifact id.
Nothing is uploaded again.

DecisionLabModel.description:
One model that answers `/v1/systemone`: a local `decide/*` row, or a
cloud alias or catalog entry of task `decision`.

context_length.description:
From its capabilities: the context it is planned against, or the
catalog's.

facts.description: What its row and its GGUF header say; `null` for a cloud model.

held.description:
The GPU hold (or a benchmark's lease) pauses it now: a GPU row while
the hold is on. A CPU row and a cloud model never are.

hold_fallback.description: The alias that answers for it while it is held, when that alias can.

limits.description: What must fit in how many tokens (§2.2's table): one or two limits.

local.description: A local aux row of kind decision.

model_id.description: The row's id, for a local model.

name.description: The public name a request asks for.

owner.description:
Who serves it, as `GET /v1/models` says (`lmgw` for a local row, the
upstream's name for a cloud model).

price.description: What prices a request to it, as the gateway prices one.

reads_images.description:
It reads images: its running server's `vision`, else an `image` among
its input modalities.

state.description:
Its container's state (`starting`, `ready`, `stopping`); `null` when
no container runs, and for a cloud model.

DecisionLimit.description: One limit a request meets on a model.

of.description:
What the number is and where it comes from ("the ubatch in effect,
set on the row").

rule.description: The rule in one sentence, with what llama.cpp answers past it.

tokens.description: The limit in tokens; `null` when it is not known.

oneOf.description:
The state and one question (with its options and the template): the
gauge's estimate is the state plus the largest question.

The span from the first option marker to the end of the prompt: the
estimate is the largest option list.

DecisionPrice.description:
What prices a request to a decision model: the rows the gateway's own
price lookup selects for its primary route (`Snapshot::sheet_for`), the
route a request takes when no fallback answers. A fallback that answers
is priced by its own rows.

fallback.description:
While a local row is held and its `hold_fallback` can answer, the
price of the alias that answers every request instead (the rows the
gateway then records it at). Absent otherwise.

local.description:
Served on this machine: free whatever rows exist (Usage records the
compute it takes, not a price).

rows.description:
Per unit, the row that prices it, each unit resolved on its own: the
alias's manual row, else the alias's catalog row, else the upstream
model's manual row, else its catalog row; a row without a usable rate
is no row. Empty for a local model, and for a cloud model no row
covers, whose cost Usage records as unknown.

unresolved.description:
Why its route did not resolve (a candidate alias picks its model per
request); `rows` is empty then.

DecisionQuestionKind.description: A question's type and its type's fields.

oneOf.description: Pick one of the options, in the order offered.
Rate on 2 to 10 levels, lowest first.

Yes or no; `yes` and `no` say what each means, both blank sends no
`criteria`.

DecisionQuestionKindInput.description: A question's type and its type's fields.

oneOf.description: Pick one of the options, in the order offered.
Rate on 2 to 10 levels, lowest first.

Yes or no; `yes` and `no` say what each means, both blank sends no
`criteria`.

DecisionShape.description: A decision model's header shape (decision-models design §3.4).

oneOf.description:
`attention.causal = false` (Laya, Julia-1): the whole prompt in one
ubatch.
Causal with a decision head (Kev, Clef): embedding mode.
Causal, answering from label logits (lev, OpenJev): a normal context.

depth.description: *D*: the prompt length the generation starts from.

distinct_token_ratio.description:
Distinct token ids over generated ones, per repetition: near 1 for
prose, low for a degenerate loop that `ignore_eos` ran into — and a
loop is what a drafter predicts perfectly, so a draft acceptance
next to a low ratio flatters it. Only where the
engine streams token ids (official llama.cpp, not ik).

energy.description:
Over first token → last token of each repetition, so the priming
prefill stays out; tokens are those generated after the first.

energy_unmeasured.description:
Why `energy` is `None` although the card reports power: a window
shorter than the GPU sampler resolves (two of its ticks, 200 ms at
the 100 ms tick), whose figure would have been the
ticks' average power times its length rather than a measurement.
`None` otherwise.

evaluated_tokens.description:
`timings.prompt_n`: the first repetition primes the cache (≈ *D*), the
later ones reuse it (a handful).

DeviceCaError.description: Why lmgw's device CA cannot be used.

kind.description: What kind of failure it is.

message.description:
The reason in a sentence, naming the file, the mode found or the
Secret Service's answer.

oneOf.description: No CA exists, and the call needed one.
The wallet's unlock prompt was declined.

A file cannot be read, does not parse, or the key does not open or
does not match the certificate.

The key file is readable by group or others, not owned by lmgw's
user, or a symbolic link.
The key is wrapped and no Secret Service answers this start.

The key is wrapped and the Secret Service holds no wrapping key for
this data directory.
The Secret Service answered with an error.

DeviceCaKeyMode.description: How `tls/ca.key` keeps the CA's key (device link design D2).

oneOf.description:
Encrypted (AES-256-GCM) under a key held in the session's Secret
Service.

Plain PKCS#8, readable by its owner only: a start without a Secret
Service (headless). The next start that reaches one wraps it.

DeviceCaState.description: Whether lmgw's device CA exists and signs.

oneOf.description:
None exists: it is created when the device listener is first turned
on.

On disk and not loaded since this start (the device listener has not
run): `fp`, `created` and `key_mode` are read from the files, the key
itself is not opened.
Loaded: its key is open and signs.
It cannot be used; `error` says why.

DeviceCaStatus.description: lmgw's device CA (device link design §2.1), as the status shows it.

cert_file.description:
The certificate's path (`tls/ca.crt` in the data directory), PEM,
readable by anyone: what `curl --cacert` takes.

certificate_pem.description:
The CA certificate, PEM: what `curl --cacert` takes and the Devices
card copies. Public like the file (`0644`) and the pin; `null` while
the CA is missing or its certificate cannot be read.

created.description:
The CA's creation day (its `notBefore`), RFC 3339 UTC; `null` with
`fp`.

error.description: Why the CA cannot be used, with state `error`.

fp.description:
`sha256:` and the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the CA certificate's
SubjectPublicKeyInfo: the pairing link's `fp`. `null` while the CA is
missing or its certificate cannot be read.

key_file.description: The key file's path (`tls/ca.key` in the data directory).

key_mode.description:
How the key file keeps the key; `null` while the CA is missing or the
key file cannot be read.

state.description: Whether the CA exists and signs.

DeviceLeafSlot.description: Which connections a server certificate serves.

oneOf.description: Every connection to a loopback address (`127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`).
Connections to one address of this machine's interfaces.

Connections to an address no interface lists: the URL-list hosts
alone.

DeviceLeafStatus.description:
One server certificate the device listener presents (device link design
§2.2).

address.description:
The local address it serves, for `interface`; `null` for `loopback`
and `shared`.

issued.description: When it was issued, RFC 3339 UTC.

names.description:
The names it carries (its subjectAltNames): its address, or the
loopback addresses and `localhost`, and every host of every device's
URL list.

renew_after.description:
From when the next connection it would serve gets a new one: half its
validity.

oneOf.description: `devices.listener` is off, or the gateway is not serving.
It serves on `urls`.

It is on and does not serve; `error` says why. The plain listener
serves on.

DeviceListenerStatus.description:
The device listener (device link design §4.1, §9.2), as the status
shows it: whether it serves, where, or why not, and what it holds open.

connections.description: Its open connections now, TLS handshakes included.

error.description:
Why it does not serve, with state `error`: a bind error naming the
address and the settings, the device CA's reason, or a port it cannot
derive.

evicted.description:
Such connections it closed since it started to make room for a newer
one, one of those two bounds reached (the oldest goes).

listen.description:
The scope it serves, or tried to: `loopback`, `all` or an address
(`devices.listen`); `null` while off.

port.description:
The port it serves, or tried to (`devices.port`, or the HTTP port's
number plus one); `null` while off.

requests.description: The requests in flight on it now (an open Chat feed is one).

sessions.description: The realtime sessions and turns running on it now.

state.description: Whether it serves.

unauthenticated.description:
Its connections that have not authenticated, now: handshakes in
progress, connections without a certificate, and connections whose
certificate opens no working device. What `devices.unauthenticated_max`
and `devices.unauthenticated_per_peer` bound.

urls.description:
What it is bound to, as `https://` base URLs: two for `loopback`
(one when the machine has no IPv6), one otherwise. Empty unless
`listening`.

DevicePaired.description:
A device's pairing link minted: `POST /api/op/key_create` with `kind:
device` (the row and its first pairing token) and `device_token` (a new
token for the same row; device link design §3.2, §5.2). The token goes to
the owner once, inside the link.

fp.description:
`sha256:` and the hex SHA-256 of the device CA's SubjectPublicKeyInfo:
the link's `fp`, which the device's enrolment pins.

id.description: The device row's `api_keys.id`; a new token keeps it.

link.description:
`lmgw-pair:?v=2&name=…&url=…[&url=…]&fp=sha256:…&token=lmgw-enrol-…`:
carries the one-time pairing token to the device. Secret while its
token lives: shown once, never logged.

local_only.description:
Paired as "this computer": the device reaches lmgw on a loopback
address only.

message.description:
What was done, for a person to read: what the device does next, and
whether the device listener reaches it from where it is.

name.description: `device:<name>`.

ok.description: Always `true`; a refusal is an error answer instead.

token_expires_at.description:
When the pairing token lapses (RFC 3339, UTC): `devices.token_minutes`
after it was minted.

urls.description:
The device's lmgw URLs: `https` base URLs of the device listener, in
the owner's order, as the link carries them and enrolment answers
them.

oneOf.description:
No key: waiting for its device to enrol with a token (or for a new
token, when its last one ended).

A key enrolled and waiting for the owner's confirmation: its every
request is refused 403 `device_unconfirmed` until then. A key kept
beside it (`kept_code`) is served until the confirmation ends it.
Enrolled and confirmed: the device is served.

Paired with a link from before TLS: its bearer key no longer works,
and it needs a new token.

DevicePairingStatus.description:
Pairing in `GET /api/status` (device link design §3.3, §9.2): the tokens
alive, and the failed enrolments of the last hour.

counted_since.description:
Since when failures are counted: the counts live in memory and start
at zero with each start of lmgw (RFC 3339 UTC).

failures_last_hour.description:
Failed enrolments (an unknown, used, lapsed or ended token) in the
last hour, from every address.

last_failure_from.description:
The address of the last failure (an IPv6 address by its /64), `null`
when none was counted.

tokens_alive.description:
The pairing tokens alive now (minted, not lapsed, not ended; a used
one stays alive for its same-key repeat): while any is, a device
listener handshake may come without a client certificate, for
enrolment alone.

DevicePairingView.description:
A device row's pairing (device link design §3.6, §9.3), as the Keys
list shows it.

cert_not_after.description:
The certificate of the key that works now: its `notAfter`, and from
when the card and the device say it lapses (two thirds of its
validity), RFC 3339 UTC.

confirm_code.description:
The confirmation code, `7F3A-91C2`, of the key that waits for the
owner's confirmation in state `enrolled`, of the confirmed key
otherwise: what the device shows, and what the owner compares and
sends with `device_confirm`.

confirmed_at.description:
When the owner confirmed the key that works now (RFC 3339 UTC); with
a key waiting, the kept key's confirmation.

contested_at.description:
When a used token of its came back with another key, and from where:
if the device did not pair, someone else holds a certificate for the
row (unconfirmed until the owner confirms it), so delete it.

enrolled_at.description:
When its last enrolment was (RFC 3339 UTC), from where (the peer
address) and with which client (the enrolment's free text, never
trusted for anything): a waiting key's, while one waits.

kept_code.description:
With a new key waiting beside the device's confirmed one (a re-pair
that kept the current key): the kept key's code. The kept key is
served until the waiting one is confirmed, which ends it.

state.description: Where its pairing stands.

token.description: Its latest pairing token, if it was ever given one.

urls.description: Its lmgw URLs, `https`, in the owner's order.

DeviceUrl.description: One URL proposed for another device.

interface.description:
The interface the address is on (`eth0`, `wg0`); empty for a
listener set to one address.

wireguard.description:
The interface is a point-to-point link (WireGuard, Tailscale), not
a LAN's.

DevicesSettings.description:
Settings → Network & access → Devices (`devices.*` in
`GET /api/settings-full`, device link design §9.1).

client_cert_days.description:
A device certificate's validity, in days (1 to 3650); the card and
the device show a notice from two thirds of it. Applies to the next
certificate issued.

enrol_refuse_per_min.description:
Failed enrolments per address (an IPv6 address by its /64) per
minute before the address is answered 429 (1 to 100000); applies at
once.

handshake_timeout_s.description:
A TLS handshake's bound, in seconds (1 to 300); applies to the next
connection.

header_timeout_s.description:
A request head's bound, and an idle kept-alive connection's wait for
the next one, in seconds (1 to 3600); applies to the next connection.

listen.description:
Where the device listener binds: `loopback` (`127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`,
while every paired device is this computer), `all` (`[::]`, every
address) or one IP address.

listener.description:
Whether the device listener runs: the TLS listener paired devices
connect to. Off until the first pairing turns it on.

port.description:
The device listener's port; `null` = the HTTP port's number plus one,
written as a number the first time the listener starts.

port_effective.description:
The port the device listener binds: `port`, else the HTTP port's
number plus one; `null` when `port` is `null` and the HTTP port is
65535 (no port above it), so the setting must name one.

server_cert_days.description:
A server certificate's validity, in days (1 to 3650); a server
certificate is re-issued from half of it, unnoticed by devices.
Applies to the next certificate issued.

token_minutes.description:
A pairing token's lifetime, in minutes (1 to 1440); applies to the
next token.

unauthenticated_max.description:
The device listener's connections that have not authenticated yet
(handshakes in progress, connections without a certificate or with
one that opens no working device), at most, from every peer together
(1 to 4096); a new one past it closes the oldest. Applies to the next
connection.

unauthenticated_per_peer.description:
The same, from one peer: an IPv4 address, an IPv6 address by its /64
(1 to 4096); a new one past it closes that peer's oldest. Applies to
the next connection.

unauthenticated_timeout_s.description:
A whole connection without a client certificate, in seconds (1 to
300); applies to the next connection.

DevicesSettingsPatch.description: The sparse patch both saves take under `devices`.

client_cert_days.description:
A device certificate's validity in days, 1 to 3650; the notice comes
at two thirds of it. Applies to the next certificate issued.

enrol_refuse_per_min.description:
Failed enrolments per address (an IPv6 address by its /64) per
minute before a 429, 1 to 100000. Applies at once.

handshake_timeout_s.description:
A TLS handshake's bound in seconds, 1 to 300. Applies to the next
connection.

header_timeout_s.description:
A request head's bound, and an idle kept-alive connection's, in
seconds, 1 to 3600. Applies to the next connection.

listen.description:
Where it binds: `loopback` (127.0.0.1 and [::1]), `all` ([::], every
address) or one IP address. Applies at once, moving it and ending its
connections.

listener.description:
The device listener: on or off. Applies at once: on binds it (making
lmgw's device CA on its first start), off closes it and ends its
connections — its feeds, realtime sessions and calls — never the
plain listener's.

port.description:
Its port, 1 to 65535. Applies at once, moving it and ending its
connections. Unset, it is the HTTP port's number plus one, written
here the first time the listener is turned on.

server_cert_days.description:
A server certificate's validity in days, 1 to 3650; it is re-issued
from half of it. Applies to the next certificate issued.

token_minutes.description:
A pairing token's lifetime in minutes, 1 to 1440. Applies to the next
token.

unauthenticated_max.description:
The device listener's connections that have not authenticated yet
(handshakes in progress included), at most, from every peer
together, 1 to 4096; a new one past it closes the oldest. Applies to
the next connection.

unauthenticated_timeout_s.description:
A whole connection without a client certificate, in seconds, 1 to
300. Applies to the next connection.

DevicesStatus.description:
`devices` in `GET /api/status` (device link design §9.2): lmgw's device
CA and the server certificates issued from it.

ca.description:
lmgw's device CA: whether it exists and is loaded, its pin and how
its key is kept, or why it cannot be used.

leaves.description:
The server certificates issued since this start, one per local
address that served a device connection (one for every loopback
address); empty until the device listener serves.

listener.description: The device listener: off, where it listens, or why it does not.

pairing.description: Pairing: the tokens alive and the failed enrolments counted.

DictatedVoice.description:
How a dictated message says it was dictated (`voice` of a send): the
facts of the transcribe answer, nothing a reply carries. Unknown fields
are refused.

asr.description: The speech-to-text alias that was asked.

asr_answered_by.description: The alias that answered in its place, when a fallback did.

via.description:
Must be `dictation`: a realtime turn is written by the bound session
and cannot be sent.

DiskInfo.description:
`container_images`' `disk` field:
`podman system df` totals plus orphaned build leftovers, shown for
information only — nothing is pruned from here.

buildah_orphans.description:
`/var/tmp/buildahNNN` dirs and `Storage` containers not yet cleaned
up.

client_name.description: MCP client name from `initialize`, when it gave one.

version.description: Empty when the requester pinned no version.

DocsSearchDefaults.description:
The stage defaults (`Settings.docs_search`) — where a request that
overrides nothing starts. None of these is a cap: every one is a
per-request parameter the playground and `docs__query` can override.

budget_tokens.description: `0` means *no budget* — every one of `limit` chunks comes back.

eval_k.description: Depth an eval run measures hit@k at when the request names no `k`.

fts_weights.description:
BM25 column weights — a stage default like any other, and one the
playground exposes, so it has to round-trip through a save.

DocsSearchPatch.description:
The Docs search stage defaults. Every field is optional so the Docs tab can
move one knob without restating the rest.

content_hash.description: Gates incremental re-ingest: unchanged pages never re-run the model.

job_id.description:
Id of the `hf_download` job currently transferring this file, if any —
what "Cancel" acts on. `None` means nothing is running for this row.

requested_revision.description:
The revision the download asks for: `main`, or the commit an audio
catalog entry pins. `None` on a row from before it was recorded (a
`main` download).

resolved_commit.description:
The commit the file on disk came from (the hub's `X-Repo-Commit`).
`None` when unknown — every row downloaded before it was recorded.

status.description:
`queued | downloading | done | failed | update_available` — a row that
claims queued/downloading with no live progress is *interrupted*
(derived, never stored).

DownloadedFrom.description: Where a downloaded weights file came from.

DraftStats.description:
Speculative decoding's draft statistics, summed over a point's requests. Present only when the
server reported them.

EditApplied.description:
One Dockerfile edit's result in a resolved preview: the run log's
"applied (N matches)" / "not matched", as data.

applied.description:
Occurrences replaced; `0` = not matched (a run fails on that when the
edit is `required`).

index.description: Position in the edit list, from 0 (an edit's `name` may be empty).

EditRole.description:
What a Dockerfile edit is for. The role is what lets the build's
own switches reach an edit that was customized: `ccache` off drops every
`ccache` and `cache` edit, whether it came
from the preset or was typed by hand.

oneOf.description:
Compiler-cache wiring: the `ccache` package, the cache mount, the
compiler launchers, the stats line.

Another build cache mount (the web UI's npm cache). Optional, and a
cache like ccache: off with it.

Build number / commit / date injection, so `--version` names what was
built even though `.git` is not in the build context.

`docker.io/` in front of a bare base image, so it resolves without a
short-name alias.
A different base-image variant (sd.cpp's `-cudnn-` dropped).
Anything else — what a hand-written edit is unless it says otherwise.

dimensions.description: Forwarded (Gemini: outputDimensionality). A route that answers with another length — llama-server has no such parameter — is refused with 400 rather than served full-length vectors.

encoding_format.description: Encoded by the gateway, whatever the upstream: base64 is the little-endian float32 bytes, as OpenAI serves it.

input.description: A string, or an array of strings. Token-id arrays are refused with 400: an alias can route to a model with another tokenizer.

embedding.description: Floats, or a base64 string when encoding_format was base64.

prompt_tokens.description: What the model reported; 0 when it reported nothing.

total_tokens.description: The same number: embedding generates nothing.

Energy.description: The energy of a measured window: a point's, summed over its repetitions.

joules.description: The whole card, idle draw included.

seconds.description: Length of the measured windows, summed.

tokens.description:
The tokens those windows produced (prefill: prompt tokens; decode:
generated tokens).

tokens_per_joule.description: `tokens / joules`; `None` when the windows measured 0 J.

tokens_per_joule_each.description:
Tokens per joule of each window on its own (one per repetition, or
per request for prefill): the spread the comparison reads as this
figure's noise. A half-second decode window right after an idle
moment is measured while the card's clocks ramp up — live, decode at
depth 64 read 2.47 and 3.01 tok/J in two runs of identical settings.
Windows the counter did not move over are left out.

EnergySource.description: Where a joule figure came from.

oneOf.description:
The driver's total-energy counter, read at both ends of the window
(NVML `nvmlDeviceGetTotalEnergyConsumption`).

Power samples integrated over the window (trapezoids), because the
counter is not available.

EnergySummary.description: The run's VRAM and energy picture.

baseline_vram_bytes.description: Device VRAM used before the bench container started.

idle_power_w.description: Mean power over the baseline window, so a view can show net energy.

source.description:
How the run's joules were measured; `None` when the GPU reports no
power at all (then `unavailable` says why).

Engine.description:
Which of the three engines lmgw runs a build produces. ik_llama.cpp is
`Llama` with its own repo preset, not an engine of its own: its images run
in the same classes.

oneOf.description: llama.cpp and ik_llama.cpp — `llama-server`.
audio.cpp — `audiocpp_server`.
stable-diffusion.cpp — `sd-server`.

id.description: The device row's `api_keys.id`; re-pairing keeps it.

name.description: The device's name as lmgw gave it, without `device:`.

refusal.description:
True when this kind is lmgw refusing, rather than an upstream or a
client failing — the two belong in different colours.

EvalRunRow.description:
One measured run. `params` is the stage parameter set it was measured under —
two runs under different parameters are not comparable, so the numbers
never travel without them.

orphaned_queries.description:
Queries whose every expected chunk is gone — they score zero for a
reason that is not "retrieval got worse".

params.description:
The stage parameters it was measured under; absent when the stored text
does not parse.

report.description: Full per-query breakdown; absent on the same terms as `params`.

Example.description:
One static example exchange: what the user says, and how the model
replies. Both sides are non-empty.

ExportAttachment.description: An attachment as the export carries it: its metadata, position and bytes.

blockers.description: For a draft: why it cannot be sent to the thread's current model.

data.description: The file's bytes, base64 (standard alphabet, padded).

extracted.description:
The text extracted from it (a PDF's pages, an office file, an audio
file's transcript); `null` when there is none.

extracted_tokens.description: The extracted text's token estimate; `null` when there is none.

hints.description:
For a draft: what it becomes on the way, sent all the same (an image
as a placeholder, a PDF's pages as its text) under a fallback that
cannot see.

kind.description: `image`, `pdf`, `text`, `audio`, ... as the upload was classified.

meta.description:
What extraction found: pages, text-less pages, class, sheets,
transcript alias or error, tokens. `{}` for an image.

mode.description:
A text-class PDF's choice, `text` or `images`; `null` when it does
not apply or is not chosen yet.

ord.description: Its position among its message's files.

ExportMessage.description:
A message as the export carries it: the columns of a stored message with
its `ir_messages` parsed, and the files sent with it.

ir_messages.description:
An agentic turn's tool calls and results as the JSON value the
record holds; `null` for a plain turn. When the record does not
parse, its raw text and `ir_messages_unparsed: true`.

ir_messages_unparsed.description:
Set (to `true`) only when `ir_messages` is the raw text of a record
that did not parse.

ExportRef.description: A folder or personality profile named in an export.

ExportThread.description:
A thread as the export carries it: the columns of the thread list's row
(`ThreadRow`) except the two derived from other rows, `last_message_at`
and `purge_at`.

kind.description: `chat` or `admin`.

temporary.description: The thread was held in memory only (a temporary chat).

ExtraChange.description: One unpinned extra's change since the last verified run.

change.description:
The badge's own wording: `"pushed"`, `"closed unmerged"`, or one
of the two "merged upstream" readings (see `reasons` of the update status).

Fallback.description: A hold fallback, and whether it is local (a usable one never is).

FallbackUnusable.description:
A named hold fallback that cannot answer: `why` is the clause the hold's
refusal names it with ("does not resolve", "is itself a local model").

FeedHold.description:
The GPU hold: whether local models are paused, and the alias that answers
for them meanwhile. The `hold` event and part of
`Hello`.

FeedPrincipal.description:
Who the feed is for: its kind and the name it is known by, without the
kind's prefix. A paired device is kind `device`, named as it was paired
("desktop", not "device:desktop"); the gateway's administrator has the
other kind: the dashboard (named `dashboard`) or an admin key (named as
the key without its prefix).

Folder.description:
A Chat folder as `GET /chat/api/folders` lists it, with its thread
counts as the caller may see them.

archive_days.description:
Days without activity before one of its threads is archived; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

devices_hidden.description:
Set when a device deleted this folder while it held threads that
device could not see: the folder stays for them, hidden from every
device, until it is shown to devices again from the dashboard. Always
`false` for a device key, which never sees such a folder.

name.description: Folder names need not be unique.

ongoing.description: `null` for a folder that is not one ongoing conversation.

purge_days.description:
Days after archiving before one of its threads is deleted; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

sort.description: The folder's place in the list.

FolderChanged.description:
`folder.created` / `folder.updated` for a folder that exists at
delivery: the folder as `GET /chat/api/folders` lists it now (its counts
as the reader may see them), with `by` beside its fields.

archive_days.description:
Days without activity before one of its threads is archived; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

by.description: Who made the change; `null` for the gateway's own.

devices_hidden.description:
Set when a device deleted this folder while it held threads that
device could not see: the folder stays for them, hidden from every
device, until it is shown to devices again from the dashboard. Always
`false` for a device key, which never sees such a folder.

name.description: Folder names need not be unique.

ongoing.description: `null` for a folder that is not one ongoing conversation.

purge_days.description:
Days after archiving before one of its threads is deleted; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

sort.description: The folder's place in the list.

FolderGone.description:
`folder.deleted`, and `folder.created` / `folder.updated` for a folder
that is gone by the time the event is delivered.

FolderOngoing.description:
The `ongoing` field of a folder: `null` for a folder that is not an
ongoing conversation.

current_thread_id.description:
The thread the conversation continues in; `null` until the first
`current` call, after its thread was deleted, moved out of the
folder or archived by hand, and, for a device key, while the thread
is out of the key's reach.

idle_minutes.description:
Minutes without a message after which the next `current` call starts
a new thread. `0`: a new thread only when a client asks for one.

FolderRef.description: A folder named by its id and name.

Forge.description: Where a build's repository lives, which decides how PR extras are found.

oneOf.description: PRs are `refs/pull/<n>/head`, details from the GitHub REST API.
MRs are `refs/merge-requests/<n>/head`, details from `/api/v4`.
No PR list and no forge API: refs from other remotes only.

ForgePr.description: One PR (GitHub) or MR (GitLab) as the extras picker shows it.

merge_commit_sha.description:
The commit the merge put on its target branch — the merge, squash or
rebase commit (GitHub `merge_commit_sha`; GitLab `merge_commit_sha`,
else `squash_commit_sha`). Empty when the forge gives none (an open
PR, an old GitLab). A build skips a merged PR as "merged upstream"
only when its base contains this commit (or the PR's head).

merged_at.description: Set once the forge reports it merged.

state.description: The forge's own spelling (`open` | `closed`).

FtsWeightsPatch.description: The four BM25 column weights, each optional like every other stage default.

FtsWeightsView.description: BM25 column weights, in `chunk_fts` column order.

path.description: Relative to models_dir — exactly what the path fields take.

GoldenCandidateRow.description:
One generated query awaiting a decision. It is **not** a golden query: an
eval never scores it, and only an accept turns it into one.

decided_at.description: Empty while it is still pending.

expected_chunk_ids.description:
The chunk it was written from — attached by code, never named by the
model.

golden_query_id.description: The golden query it became, when it was accepted.

model.description: The model that wrote it — the corpus's pinned ingest model.

rationale.description: The model's sentence about why that chunk answers it.

GpuBackend.description:
The GPU backend a build targets. Labelled **GPU backend** on the
Backends page, so it does not read as the page's own subject. Picks the
preset's Dockerfile candidate.

GpuIdentity.description:
The GPU the run used, as far as the sampler sees it. Sums and maxima over the visible
devices.

clock_events.description: The OR of every sample's clock-event reasons.

name.description: The first device's name (a comparison key).

telemetry.description: The GPU probe's own label (`NVML (driver …)`, or why there is none).

throttled.description:
Whether any of those is a throttling reason: NVML's software power cap
(`0x4`), hardware slowdown (`0x8`), software or hardware thermal
slowdown (`0x20`, `0x40`) or power-brake slowdown (`0x80`). Idle, the
applications-clocks setting, sync boost and the display clock are
states, not throttling. A run that throttled reports the throttled
numbers.

GroupApplied.description:
A group, `apply`: every running member recreated, and the static checks
over every enabled model in scope.

held.description: Stopped and not started again because the GPU hold is on.

Left running untouched because the GPU hold would not let them start
again.

GroupStarted.description: A group, `start`: only the models flagged warm_start are started.

held.description: Left alone because the GPU hold is on.

vram.description: The GPU ledger, whole even when one group was asked about.

busy.description: Still serving requests and left running; `override` forces them.

Headline.description:
The headline numbers of one run, each `None` when the run did not
measure it.

decode_deep_tok_s.description: Decode tok/s at the deepest point, *D_max*.

decode_tokens_per_joule.description: Decode tokens per joule at depth 64.

load_vram_bytes.description: VRAM the load took (after load minus the baseline).

prefill_tok_s.description: Prefill tok/s at 2048 tokens, or the nearest measured length.

prefill_tokens.description: The length it was measured at.

HelloCert.description: `Hello::cert`: the device certificate's dates, RFC 3339 UTC.

notice_after.description:
From when the device says "this certificate lapses on `<not_after>`;
pair it again before then" (two thirds of its validity).

HfCompanion.description: A file `hf_add` queued beside the weights.

HfUpdatesChecked.description:
`POST /api/op/hf_set` with `action: check_updates`: the tracked downloads of
one class compared with the hub.

errors.description: One sentence per file the hub could not be asked about.

ok.description:
`false` when a file could not be compared (`errors` is not empty); the
answer is still a success, for the files that could.

updates_available.description:
How many finished downloads now differ from the hub's copy; each is
flagged `update_available`.

HoldFallbackMode.description:
Per-model override of the GPU hold's fallback lookup: whether a held
request against this row falls back to the global chat alias, refuses
outright, or names its own alias.

oneOf.description:
Chat: fall through to `settings.hold.fallback_alias`. Aux/audio: no
fallback — they never inherit the global (a different embedding
model silently corrupts a vector index).

Refuse a held request against this row even if a global fallback is
configured.
Use this row's own `hold_fallback` alias.

HoldSettingsDto.description:
The GPU hold settings. `active` is
reported here but never settable through `SettingsFullPatch` — it is
toggled only through the `hold_set` op, because engaging it has the side
effect of stopping containers.

HoldSettingsPatch.description:
The GPU hold's global fallback. Carries no `active` field: engaging the
hold runs the GPU sweep, a side effect a generic settings patch must not
have, so the switch itself is flipped only through the `hold_set`
operation. A patch that names `active` is rejected, like any other field
this route does not carry.

fallback_alias.description:
`""` clears it back to "refuse"; otherwise validated (must resolve,
must not be local) before it is stored.

logical_cpus.description: Online logical CPUs, SMT siblings included.

physical_cores.description:
Physical cores, or the logical count when the topology is unreadable
(`source`).

source.description:
`topology` (counted from the kernel's CPU topology) | `logical` (the
topology could not be read, so the logical count stands in).

HostSettings.description:
Settings → MCP (`mcp.*` in `GET /api/settings-full`): the host link's
limits, each explicit on the link's WebSocket (§5.1), and the MCP Tasks
poll interval.

host_max_frame_mb.description: The largest frame, in MiB; `0` = bounded by `host_max_message_mb`.

host_max_message_mb.description:
The largest message a device may send, in MiB; `0` = no bound of its
own (a frame is then bounded by `host_max_frame_mb`). Not `0`
together with `host_max_frame_mb`. A full-desktop screenshot is the
expected large message.

host_ping_interval_s.description:
Seconds between the link's pings; a ping with no pong for a whole
interval closes the link. `0` = no pings, and no bound on a device
that stopped answering.

task_poll_interval_s.description:
Seconds between two `tasks/get` of an MCP task whose server suggests
no `pollInterval` of its own (MCP Tasks design §5.2); a server's
status notifications act at once. At least `1`.

ImageCapabilities.description:
One sd-server's own answer about the pipeline it loaded.

Every field defaults, because this is the one payload in the class that
comes from a moving container tag: a build that stops reporting a number
must leave the rest readable rather than fail the frame.

supported_modes.description:
`["img_gen"]`, `["img_gen","vid_gen"]` — what the loaded pipeline can
actually do, as opposed to what the row claims.

ImageEditsRequest.description: Refused unless the resolved model's row has its edit pipeline enabled.

image.description: One or more image files. lmgw relays every multipart field named image verbatim, with no cardinality check of its own.

ImageFeatures.description:
Which optional inputs the loaded pipeline admits to accepting. Not an edit
gate — the row's `edit` column is.

ImageGenForm.description:
Everything the lab's two panels collect, as typed. Numbers travel as the
strings the inputs hold: an empty field means "say nothing about this", not
zero, and a malformed one has to be reportable as a message rather than
silently become a default.

model.description:
The public alias — `image/<id>` for a local row, the alias for a cloud
one. Rewritten to the concrete upstream id by the route itself.

seed.description:
Blank says nothing (sd-server's own default is a fixed 42); `-1` is its
spelling for "random each run".

ImageGenFormInput.description:
Everything the lab's two panels collect, as typed. Numbers travel as the
strings the inputs hold: an empty field means "say nothing about this", not
zero, and a malformed one has to be reportable as a message rather than
silently become a default.

model.description:
The public alias — `image/<id>` for a local row, the alias for a cloud
one. Rewritten to the concrete upstream id by the route itself.

seed.description:
Blank says nothing (sd-server's own default is a fixed 42); `-1` is its
spelling for "random each run".

ImageGenerationsRequest.description: Other keys are forwarded for a cloud image upstream.

prompt.description: May carry a trailing <sd_cpp_extra_args>{…}</sd_cpp_extra_args> block of raw sd.cpp CLI arguments; the dashboard's Image lab builds this block and is the reference for its contents.

ImageGenerationsResponse.description: The upstream's answer, relayed as it sends it: each image carries what response_format asked for, plus whatever else the upstream adds (revised_prompt).

items.description: One image: b64_json, or url when the request asked for response_format url (an upstream's default, dall-e's, for instance).

ImageLabEditRequest.description: multipart/form-data. The body size is not limited.

form.description: The form as a JSON string: the ImageGenForm the generate route takes as its body, with optionally `image` and `mask` naming kept pictures ({id, name}, an artifact the lab store keeps) in place of an upload.

image.description: The picture to edit; stands in for the form's `image` ref. One of the two is required.

ImageLabForm.description:
A group's form: the page's form, and for an edit its picture and mask as
kept files. Also what an edit's `form` part takes, so a re-opened edit
names its kept picture instead of uploading it again; an `image` or
`mask` part of the upload stands in for the ref.

image.description: An edit's picture, kept; `null` for a generation.

mask.description: An edit's mask, kept; `null` without one.

model.description:
The public alias — `image/<id>` for a local row, the alias for a cloud
one. Rewritten to the concrete upstream id by the route itself.

seed.description:
Blank says nothing (sd-server's own default is a fixed 42); `-1` is its
spelling for "random each run".

ImageLabModel.description:
One model the Image lab can generate with: a local `image/<id>` row, or a
cloud alias whose upstream catalog says it draws. `C` is the shape of the
probed capabilities: the gateway fills in its own, a reader (and the API
document) uses `ImageCapabilities`.

args.description:
The flags a local row's container is started with (`width`, `height`,
`steps`, `cfg_scale`, `sampling_method` are the form's defaults when
set); `null` for a cloud alias.

image_capabilities.description:
What the running container reported about its loaded pipeline: the
samplers, schedulers, size bounds and LoRAs on disk. `null` until a
container has been probed.

local.description: A local row of this gateway, not a cloud alias.

model_id.description: The local row's model id; `null` for a cloud alias.

modes.description:
A local row's pipelines (`img_gen`, `vid_gen`, ...), as the operator
declared them; `null` for a cloud alias.

name.description: The alias to send as `model`.

notes.description: What the gateway noticed about the model, one sentence each.

owner.description: The upstream that serves it (`local` for the gateway's own rows).

state.description:
A local row's container state (`starting`, `ready`, `stopping`);
`null` when it has none running, and for a cloud alias.

task.description: The model's task, as `GET /v1/models` reports it.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems the running container's start found.

ImageLoraRow.description:
One row of the optional LoRA table. `<lora:…>` prompt tags are refused by
every sd.cpp family, so a LoRA is this structured field or nothing.

multiplier.description: Blank leaves the server's own multiplier in place.

path.description:
A name from the probed `loras` list, or a path the server can resolve
under its `--lora-model-dir`.

ImageLoraRowInput.description:
One row of the optional LoRA table. `<lora:…>` prompt tags are refused by
every sd.cpp family, so a LoRA is this structured field or nothing.

multiplier.description: Blank leaves the server's own multiplier in place.

path.description:
A name from the probed `loras` list, or a path the server can resolve
under its `--lora-model-dir`.

ImageModel.description:
An image model row — one stable-diffusion.cpp pipeline.

The two JSON-map fields stay dynamic on purpose, exactly as the server
types them: sd.cpp adds a model family and its flag every few weeks, and
the keys are validated against the container image's own `--help` rather
than against any enum on either side of this wire.

args.description:
Runtime + default-generation flags, same key convention. A `true`
renders as a bare switch.

capabilities_override.description: An alias's capabilities override for the derived `/v1/models` capability facts.

edit.description: The pipeline takes reference images and may serve `/v1/images/edits`.

extra_run_args.description: Per-model `podman run` args override; `None` inherits the class's.

files.description:
Flag key → path relative to the image models dir. Exactly one of
`model` / `diffusion_model` is present on a valid row.

hold_fallback_mode.description:
`inherit` | `none` | `alias`. `inherit` means "no fallback" for this
class — an image row never inherits the global chat alias.

idle_seconds.description: Seconds idle before the container is stopped; `0` never reaps.

image.description:
Per-model container image override; `None` inherits the image class
settings' image.

peak_extra_bytes.description:
The learned transient peak: what one generation was measured to need
above this pipeline's idle residency. Written by
the gateway, not by the editor — a `files` or `args` change resets it
to `None`, because a different pipeline has a different peak.

peak_learned_at.description: When that figure was observed; `None` whenever the peak is.

extra_run_args.description: `podman run` args override, one entry per argument; null inherits.

files.description: Flag key to path under the image models dir.

files_present.description: For each key of `files`, whether the file (or directory) exists.

peak_extra_bytes.description:
Bytes one generation was measured to need above idle residency;
null until one has run.

public_name.description: The name clients call it by, with the image prefix.

ImageProvenance.description:
An image's build provenance: read
from the `dev.lmgw.*` OCI labels, so an image stays self-describing even
after its `builds`/`build_runs` rows are gone.

base.description: Base SHA the run built from (`dev.lmgw.base`).

build_name.description:
The build's name as it is now — its slug when it has no name — read
from the builds table, so "follows <build>" needs no second call.
`None` once the build is deleted (the labels outlive it).

extras.description:
The extras merged in, each with its resolved SHA (`dev.lmgw.extras`,
stored on the image as JSON) — the same
shape a run's `inputs.resolved` carries.

instance.description:
The lmgw instance that built it (`dev.lmgw.instance`: one per data
dir, so a dev instance's images are told from production's). Empty
on an image built before the label existed.

other_instance.description:
Built by another lmgw instance than the one answering. Its build and
run ids are that instance's, so `build_id` and `run_id` are 0 and
`build_name` is `None` — the provenance is the labels' alone.

old_id.description:
The image ID the reference named before the pull; `None` when it was
not on this machine.

ImagePullResult.description:
The result of a finished `image_pull` job (stored on its job row). A pull
replaces no running container: `used_by` is who still runs (or names) the
old image, for the page's "Recreate N running containers" offer.

log.description: podman's whole output, line by line.

old_digests.description: `sha256:…` digests podman recorded for the reference before and after.

updated.description: The reference now names a different image than before.

args.description:
Runtime + default-generation flags for the prefilled row, already in
`ImageModel.args` shape.

installed.description: Every component is already on disk.

partial.description: Some but not all components are on disk or downloading.

served.description: An image model row already names this recipe's primary file.

total_bytes.description: Bytes of the default file set, on disk.

vram_note.description:
Measured VRAM where a spike measured it, and the word "unmeasured"
where none did — never a number derived from the file sizes.

ImageRecipeAlternative.description: A different file for the same component — the quantizations the repo ships.

present.description: This alternative is the file already on disk.

ImageRecipeComponent.description: One file of a pipeline, under the `files` key it fills.

dest_path.description:
Path relative to the image models dir once downloaded — what the row's
`files` value is.

done.description: A tracked download for it finished.

download_id.description:
Tracked download row id, when there is one — join against
`GET /api/hf/downloads` for live progress.

downloading.description: A tracked download exists for it and has not finished.

gated.description: The hub refuses this repo without a token that accepted the licence.

present.description: The file is on disk under the image models dir.

shared_with.description:
Display names of the other recipes that name this exact file. A
component is shared on purpose (the second recipe to want it finds it
on disk), but it also means one recipe's download shows up under every
neighbour — this is what lets a card say whose download it is watching.

ImageRecipeRow.description:
The prefilled row an "add from recipe" hands to the editor — the field
names `POST /api/op/image_model_set` (and `lmgw__image_model_set`) take.

ImageSettings.description:
The image class settings: the same fields as the chat/aux class settings
and no engine ones. sd-server has no config file, so everything
per-process is a flag in some row's `args`.

request_timeout_seconds.description:
Per-request ceiling for the class, in seconds. 0 = the maximum possible — no deadline of
lmgw's own.

ImageSettingsPatch.description:
The image class's patch. Shaped like `RouterSettingsPatch` — the four
fields are the same four — but kept separate rather than reusing it,
because the two types are not the same settings struct and a shared patch
would make `image.backend` a compile error away from existing.

ImageTestPassed.description: An image pipeline that drew its probe image.

bytes.description: The first image's size in bytes.

ok.description: Always `true`.

output_format.description: What the server said it encoded; null when it says nothing.

model_id.description:
Which model row: set for `model_override`, and for a
`running_container` or `stopped_container` that is one of lmgw's model
containers (read from its labels, else matched by its name) — with
`class`, what the `container` op's `apply` recreates. `None` for a
container that is no model's (an agent's, or anything else on the
machine).

ImageUseKind.description:
How something is using an image: what
`container_image_delete` refuses to delete out from under, and what
the promote success panel offers to recreate.

oneOf.description:
A container that exists but is not running — exited, created, or a
buildah working container (`podman ps -a --external`). It keeps its
image from being removed all the same.

embed_alias.description: The name on *this* gateway that routes there, when one does.

embed_model.description: The embedding identity the corpus is pinned to.

anyOf.description: The model heard the turn's audio.
The model read the speech-to-text transcript.

InputPath.description: How a voice turn's words reached the chat model.

JobRow.description:
One background job. `done`/`total` are in the kind's own unit (bytes for
`hf_download`, documents for an ingest, …) and `stage` names what is
happening; `total` is absent when the total genuinely isn't known yet.

detail.description: Kind-specific payload; the generic feed does not interpret it.

key.description: Dedup key scoped to the kind (`hf:<download row id>`).

kind.description: `hf_download | ingest | re_embed | eval_run | golden_gen`.

id.description: Absent on a notification (e.g. notifications/initialized); string or number otherwise.

method.description: e.g. initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read, notifications/initialized.

anyOf.description:
Search before every turn and send the excerpts with the user's
message.

Give the model the knowledge search tools; it searches when it
decides to.

KbMode.description: How a thread's knowledge bases reach the model.

KeptImage.description:
A tag that was left in place, and why: one a `keep_runs` prune kept, or one a `build_set`
delete with `delete_images` did not remove (in use, a name from outside
the build, a dev instance).

KeyCreated.description:
`POST /api/op/key_create` for a client or an owner key: the new row, and
its key in the clear.

A device key answers `DevicePaired` instead. The wrapper
`KeyCreateAnswer` is the document's description of the one op; a reader
knows the `kind` it sent and reads that kind's type.

key.description:
The key. Secret. A client key's is shown here and nowhere else (only
its hash is stored); an owner key's stays readable with `key_reveal`.

message.description: What was done, for a person to read.

name.description:
The key's name; an owner key's carries the `owner:` prefix the server
writes.

ok.description: Always `true`; a refusal is an error answer instead.

KeyMap.description:
A `files` or `args` map as a patch carries it, the image class's map
counterpart of the list-valued run arguments.

Two spellings for one map, and both are load-bearing. `/api/op` and the
dashboard send a real JSON object, because that is what the row stores.
The MCP plane cannot: its schemas are flat scalars on purpose (a tool
whose arguments need hand-built JSON is a tool a small local model cannot
call reliably), which is the same reason `capabilities_override` accepts a
JSON *string* there. So a text block of `key = value` lines — the syntax
printed by `sd-server --help` — is accepted wherever the object is.

KeyRow.description: One key on the Keys & policy table. `GET /api/usage/keys`

device_tools.description:
Client and device keys: the device-hosted labels whose tools the key
reaches (`["kai"]`), whatever its tool scope's mode, which then
filters those tools as any server's. A label no device hosts now is
kept and reaches nothing until one does: compare it with the device
rows' `hosts_label`. Empty for every other kind.

hosts_label.description:
Devices only: the label it may host MCP tools under; `null` without
a hosting grant.

kind.description:
`key` | `internal` | `agent` | `owner` | `device` — an internal
identity is budgetable but can never authenticate anything; an owner
key holds every capability; a device is a paired client app.

last_seen_at.description:
Devices only: when one of its long-lived connections (the Chat
feed, a voice session, its tool link) last opened or closed,
RFC 3339 UTC.

online.description:
Devices only: which of its connections are open now — `feed`,
`voice`, `tools`, in that order. Empty means offline.

open_links.description:
Devices only: how many connections of each kind in `online` are
open, in the same order. More than one of a kind is a client that
opened another before its last one closed.

pairing.description:
Devices only: its pairing over the device link (device link design
§3, §9.3) — its token, its enrolment and the code to confirm, a
contested token, its certificate's dates and its URLs. `null` for
every other kind.

reaches.description:
Devices with a hosting grant only: every principal that reaches the
hosted label's tools (client-apps design §5.6, L16 as changed
2026-10-15) — `owner`, the device itself, each key and device whose
`device_tools` grants the label, and each agent whose manifest names
it — as a sentence each ("owner", "device 'desktop' (hosts it)", "key
'ci'", "agent 'board'"). Empty without a grant.

self_admin.description:
Devices only: the device's level of lmgw's admin tools — `off`,
`read_only` (it reads lmgw's configuration and state) or `full` (it
also changes it, and may register programs that run on the gateway's
machine). Above `off` it sees and uses the Chat threads and folders
that carry the self-admin toolset (`lmgw`); at `full` it may also
attach the toolset and change such threads and folders. The
self-admin level in Settings caps what the tools may do. Admin Chat
stays hidden from every device. `off` for every other kind.

spent_micro.description: Spend so far in the current budget period.

spent_unknown_requests.description:
What that figure does **not** cover — the same obligation every other
money total on this plane carries. Without it the per-key meter would be
the one number on the page that cannot state its own remainder.

tool_scope_mode.description:
`all` | `allow` | `deny` over exposed MCP tool names — which tools the
key sees on `/mcp` and may attach in a `/v1/responses` run. Only a
client key's is read: an agent's tools are its manifest's, and an owner
key is not scoped.

KnowledgeBase.description: A knowledge base as every route shows it.

embed_alias.description: The embedding model alias the base was created with.

embed_context.description: The embedding model's context in tokens, when the gateway knows it.

embed_dims.description: The vector length of the pinned model.

embed_input_limit.description:
What one embedding input may hold, `min(context, ubatch)` for a local
model; `chunk_tokens` (heading path included) is checked against it.

embed_model.description: The embedding model the base is pinned to.

embed_resolvable.description:
Whether a model on this gateway still resolves to the pin. When not,
searches fall back to keywords and new files cannot be embedded.

embed_upstream.description: The upstream the alias resolved to when the base was pinned.

job.description: The live job on the base, or the last one that ran.

mcp_visible.description: Whether the `kb__*` tools on `/mcp` may search this base.

name.description: Unique across the bases.

notes.description: One sentence each: what a person should know about the base now.

resident_bytes.description:
What the base's vectors cost resident in memory: embedded chunks x
dimensions x 2.

status.description:
`ready` or `re_embed_required` (the vectors no longer match the pinned
model; Resume fills them in).

vision_alias.description: Empty: text-less PDF pages are skipped and counted.

KnowledgeCounts.description: A base's file and chunk counts.

embedded.description: Chunks that have a vector; `chunks - embedded` are waiting for one.

file_sha.description: The sha256 of the file version the chunk was cut from.

rerank_skipped.description:
Present (and true) when the rerank stage ran but did not score this
excerpt (its query + chunk pair was over the reranker's input limit):
`score` is its fused score and it ranks behind the reranked ones.

score.description:
The final order's score: the reranker's when it ran, the fused
(reciprocal-rank) score otherwise.

span_start.description: Byte range in the file's extracted text.

tokens.description: Counted over heading path and text.

error.description: Why the last ingest failed.

kind.description: What the bytes were sniffed as.

name.description: The name it was uploaded under (a label, never a path).

pages.description: Pages, slides or sheets, when the file has them.

skipped_pages.description: Text-less PDF pages that were skipped (no vision model on the base).

KnowledgeUploadRequest.description: multipart/form-data with one part per file.

file.description: One file; send as many parts as there are files. The part's field name does not matter, its file name names the file.

LabArtifactRole.description: Whether an artifact is a group's input or a run's output.

oneOf.description:
Sent with the group's requests (an image a decision model reads),
shared by its cells.
What a run produced (a generated image, a speech clip).

LabArtifactView.description: One artifact: media bytes kept as a file named by their sha256.

data_url_head.description:
An input that came as a data URL: its head as typed, everything
before the comma (`data:image/x-receipt;name=a.png;base64`). A request
sends it as `<head>,<base64 of the bytes>`; `null` for bytes that came
as bytes.

href.description:
Where the bytes are: `/labs/api/artifacts/{id}` from the API, the
file's path inside the zip in an export.

mime.description: The media type, sniffed from the bytes.

name.description: The upload's name, or the one lmgw gave an output.

ord.description: Its place among the group's inputs or the run's outputs.

run_id.description: The run that produced it; `null` for a group's input.

sha256.description: The sha256 of the bytes, which names the file.

LabBatchItem.description: What makes a group an item of a set run (labs-store design §3.1).

expected.description:
The expected answers, per question id, as the store keeps a label:
the option's name (`choice`), the level's index (`score`), `yes` or
`no` (`noul`). Empty when the item is not labelled.

item_ix.description: The item's place in the run's file, from 0.

key.description:
The item's own key, from the mapping's `key` column; `null` without
one.

LabCell.description:
One cell of a group's plan: the model it asks and the variant of the
form it sends. The cells run in plan order, one run each.

model.description: The public name asked.

variant.description:
The lab's name for what was sent: the Decision lab's `as_written`,
`no_descriptions` or `reversed`.

LabError.description:
How this plane answers a failure: `{"error": "..."}`, plus the `code` of
a refusal that has one.

code.description:
A machine-readable word, on the refusals that have one (for example
`dev_shared_models_dir`).

LabExportFormat.description: The file format of an export.

oneOf.description:
Lossless: one `lmgw.lab.v1` line per group; a zip with the files when
the scope has artifacts.
The lab's flat table.

The Image and Audio labs' files under readable names: one group's
one file as it is, else a zip of the files and a `manifest.jsonl`
(`LabFilesManifestLine`). The Decision lab makes no files (a 400).

LabFileKind.description: What a file of the export is.

oneOf.description:
A run's output as the store keeps it: a picture, a speech file, a
task's audio.

A run's streamed or raw PCM speech, kept as it arrived and written as
a WAV with the PCM format the form held (the gateway's
`x-lmgw-sample-rate` wins over its rate).
A transcription's or a task's text answer, as UTF-8 text.

LabFileRef.description:
A file the store keeps, as a form names it: the artifact's id and the
name it came with. A re-opened form sends it back, so a re-ask uploads
nothing again.

name.description: The upload's file name.

LabFilesInput.description:
One input of the group a file's run read: an upload to transcribe, an
edit's picture. Named here, not carried in the zip: it is the owner's own
file, and the JSONL export carries it.

name.description: The upload's name.

LabFilesManifestLine.description: One line of a files zip's manifest: a file, and the run it came from.

answered_by.description: Which model answered: a fallback's alias when one did.

artifact_id.description:
The kept artifact the file is (or, for a WAV, was made from); `null`
for a transcript.

file.description:
The file's path inside the zip:
`<group id>-<model>-<voice or task>-<first words>.<ext>`.

inputs.description: The group's inputs the run read, which the zip does not carry.

missing.description:
The artifact's file was not in the data dir when the export was
written: the zip does not carry it, and `MISSING.txt` names it.

model.description: The model asked.

parameters.description:
The request as sent: its JSON, or for an upload the multipart
summary (`LabMultipartSummary`); a request that is no JSON as its
text.

run_id.description: The run; `null` for a run the store could not keep.

sha256.description: That artifact's sha256, which names its file in the data dir.

size.description:
The file's size in the zip, in bytes; for a missing file, the kept
artifact's.

task.description:
The Audio lab's task (`tts`, `asr`, ...), the Image lab's
`generate` or `edit`.

text.description:
The text the run was given: what was spoken, the prompt; `null`
when it was given none.

voice.description: The voice a speech run asked; `null` for anything else.

LabGroupView.description: What one click in a lab produced, or one item of a set run.

form.description:
The lab's form as the lab held it (the Decision lab's
`DecisionForm`), with its media as the group's input artifacts.

in_flight.description:
A cell of it is being answered now: its request is out and its run
not in yet. A group with no run that is not in flight was stopped.
Deleting a group in flight is the 409 `in_flight`.

item.description: The set run it is an item of; `null` for a group of the history.

override.description:
The request override, as typed (its image data URLs as
`lab-artifact:<id>`), when one was in effect.

plan.description:
The cells, in run order. A group with fewer runs than cells was
stopped.

runs.description: The runs so far, in cell order.

title.description: Derived once from the form: the state's first line, a prompt.

LabKind.description: Which lab a group belongs to; the `{lab}` of `/labs/api/{lab}/*`.

oneOf.description: The Decision lab's questions, model and thresholds.
The Image lab's form: the model, the prompt and every setting.
The Audio lab's speech panel and the PCM format of a stream.

LabRunView.description: One dispatch to one `/v1` route and what came back.

answered_by.description:
Which model answered: `x-lmgw-fallback` when a fallback did, else the
model asked.

artifacts.description: What the run produced, in order.

cell.description: Its index in the group's plan.

error_code.description:
A failure's code: the envelope's `lmgw_code`, else its `code` when
that is a string, else its `type` (llama.cpp's numeric `code` only
repeats the status), else the numeric `code`.

headers.description: The `x-lmgw-*` headers the route stamped on its answer.

http_status.description: The route's HTTP status, whatever it was.

id.description:
`null` for a run the store could not keep: the cell's answer is still
here, and `store_error` beside it says why.

input_tokens.description: The answer's input tokens, when it reported them.

latency_ms.description: How long the dispatch took in the gateway, answer read included.

output_tokens.description: The answer's output tokens, when it reported them.

request.description:
The request as sent, as text, except that each image data URL is
`lab-artifact:<id>`.

response.description:
The answer as received, as text; `null` when it was no text and is an
output artifact instead.

LabVoice.description: One voice name of a model.

kind.description:
Where the name comes from: a preset, a library clip, a shipped voice,
an embedding, or a name only the model's own server reported.

send.description:
Where lmgw puts the name in the engine's request: `voice`, or
`options.voice_id` for a native voice of a family that reads that.

transcript.description:
For a library clip: whether its transcript is recorded. Absent for
every other kind.

LabVoiceKind.description: Where a voice name comes from.

oneOf.description: A preset of the model's row.
A clip of the voice library (when the class's voice directory is it).
A voice the model's package ships.
A voice embedding file in the package's `embeddings/` folder.

A name only the model's own server reported: a running container
(or a remote upstream) knows it, lmgw's catalog does not.

LabVoicesSource.description: Where the list of `GET /audio-lab/api/voices` was read.

oneOf.description:
lmgw's own catalog (the model's presets, its package's voices, the
voice library), plus the names a running container added.
A remote upstream, asked: it has no container and no catalog here.

LadderTest.description:
A ladder row's test: every rung loaded and probed in turn, then the
model stopped.

ok.description: Every tested rung passed.

reset_to_base.description:
The model was stopped again so the next request starts at the base;
false when other traffic kept it busy.

rungs.description: The rungs tested, in order; a failure ends the list.

top_rung.description: How many rungs the ladder has.

was_running_rung.description: The rung the model was on before the test, when it was running.

LanguageNote.description:
A speech model its language does not reach as set — the ASR the spoken
language, the TTS the reply language: a thread's `voice_resolved.language_notes`,
and Settings' `chat_voice_language_notes` for the Chat's own models.

message.description:
The whole sentence the page shows: the model, then what it does
("text-to-speech model 'audio/…' takes no language: …").

key.description:
The configuration it was read under. A row whose configuration has
changed since keeps the figure but is not charged by it.

learned_at.description: When it was read (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, UTC).

LiveTurn.description:
A turn answering a thread now, who started it, and whether it is a
bound realtime session's voice turn.

LiveVoice.description:
A realtime session bound to a thread now, and who bound it ("the
dashboard", "device 'phone'").

code.description: The HTTP status, repeated in the body as llama.cpp does.

lmgw_code.description: lmgw's own machine-readable error code, e.g. gpu_hold, gpu_benchmark.

LlamaParams.description:
The full llama-server parameter surface of a local model row.
`None`/`false` = flag omitted from the rendered preset.

kv_unified.description:
`--kv-unified` (true) / `--no-kv-unified` (false); `None` leaves
llama-server's default (unified exactly when `parallel` is unset).

kv_unified_per_slot.description: `--kv-unified-per-slot`: per-request context cap on a unified row.

n_predict.description:
`--n-predict`: the most tokens one response may generate. `None` =
llama-server's own default (-1, unbounded). This is the number
`/v1/models` reports as `max_output_tokens`.

LlamaProps.description:
The facts a llama.cpp server reports about its loaded model, read once per start,
climb and adoption. Every field is optional,
and `None` is unknown — the server did not say — never `false`.

audio.description: `modalities.audio`: the server loaded a projector that hears.

build_info.description: `b<number>-<commit>` on official builds; ik_llama.cpp sends none.

caps.description:
`chat_template_caps`, the template's own booleans; empty on
ik_llama.cpp, which sends none of them.

vision.description: `modalities.vision`: the server loaded a projector that sees.

LoadResult.description: The load phase, measured by the integration around `podman run`.

LocalChain.description: One local (chat) model's full path from download to container.

aliases.description: Enabled explicit aliases routing here through a llama-server upstream.

file_exists.description: The GGUF was found by the models-dir scan.

hf_repo.description: `<org>/<repo>` when the GGUF is a tracked HF download, else empty.

hf_status.description:
HF row status (`done | queued | downloading | failed |
update_available`), empty when the file was not downloaded by lmgw.

public_name.description: Client-facing name (prefix applied), meaningful only when `public`.

capabilities_override.description:
An alias's capabilities override for the derived `/v1/models` capability facts: a JSON
object with optional keys `capabilities`, `max_output_tokens`, `notes`. `None` = no
override.

extra_run_args.description:
Per-model `podman run` args override; `None` inherits the chat
class settings' `extra_run_args`.

gguf_path.description: Relative to the models dir — never an in-container `/models/…` path.

hold_fallback.description:
The alias to route to while the GPU is held, meaningful only when
`hold_fallback_mode` is `alias`.

image.description:
Per-model container image override;
`None` inherits the chat class settings' image.

ladder.description:
Ladder rungs above the base; empty = not a ladder. Absent in frames from before this
field existed.

warm_start.description: Start this model's own container at app launch.

LocalModelDetail.description:
`GET /api/local-model?id=|model_id=` — full stored record plus derived
health for the editor.

advisories.description:
Configuration that loads and serves but misbehaves under some input
(a large image, say). Apart from `problems` because the model starts.

capabilities_override.description:
An alias's capabilities override for the derived `/v1/models` capability facts: a JSON
object with optional keys `capabilities`, `max_output_tokens`, `notes`. `None` = no
override.

downloaded_from.description: The download this file came from, when the downloader fetched it.

extra_args.description: One entry per llama-server argument (round-trips with the patch field).

extra_run_args.description:
Per-model `podman run` args override, one entry per argument (round-trips
with the patch field); `None` inherits the chat class settings'
`extra_run_args`.

image.description:
Per-model container image override;
`None` inherits the chat class settings' image.

ladder.description:
Ladder rungs above the base; empty = not a ladder. The editor's ladder table reads
it.

licence.description: The licence the GGUF header states; null when it states none.

problems.description: Static findings; empty means "nothing obviously wrong", not "loads".

rungs.description:
Every rung's own command line, per-slot context and switchover;
`null` on a row that is not a ladder.

warm_start.description: Start this model's own container at app launch.

LocalModelView.description: A local chat model row plus its client-facing public name.

licence.description:
The licence the row's GGUF header states; null when it states none
or the file cannot be read.

description.description: A toolset's purpose; "" for a server.

kind.description: builtin: lmgw's own toolsets (lmgw, for owner credentials only; docs; kb); server: a registered MCP server; agent: a service agent's tools.

name.description: A server's configured name; a toolset's label.

server_label.description: What goes into a {"type": "mcp", "server_label"} tool on /v1/realtime or /v1/responses: a built-in toolset's label, a registered server's tool prefix, else its name.

name.description: The server's own name for the tool: its exposed name minus the <prefix>__ namespace.

description.description: A toolset's purpose; "" for a server.

kind.description: builtin: lmgw's own toolsets (lmgw, for owner credentials only; docs; kb); server: a registered MCP server; agent: a service agent's tools.

name.description: A server's configured name; a toolset's label.

server_label.description: What goes into a {"type": "mcp", "server_label"} tool on /v1/realtime or /v1/responses: a built-in toolset's label, a registered server's tool prefix, else its name.

agent_id.description:
Set for an agent's own registration (container-runtime §3.3), so the
MCP page can say who owns a row it must not offer to edit; `null` for
every row an owner made.

device.description:
A `device` row's device, by its short name (`desktop`); `null` for
every other row.

device_key_id.description: A `device` row's key id (`api_keys.id`); `null` for every other row.

env.description: `KEY=value` lines, as stored — a server's credentials usually live here.

headers.description: `Name: value` lines, as stored — an HTTP server's bearer lives here.

open_tasks.description:
The MCP tasks this server runs for Chat threads now, at list time
(MCP Tasks design §6): started by a call of one of its `required`
tools and not ended yet. No cap (T9); a server with open tasks is
never reaped for idleness (T17).

status.description:
`ready | connecting | error | stopped` at list time; live updates come
from the SSE `mcp` frame.

transport.description:
`stdio | http | sse | device`. A `device` row is a paired device's
hosted tools (client-apps design §5.2): created by its hosting grant,
connected while the device's host link is open.

McpSettingsPatch.description: The sparse patch the dashboard's settings save takes under `mcp`.

host_max_frame_mb.description:
In MiB; `0` = bounded by `host_max_message_mb`. Not `0` together with
it.

host_max_message_mb.description:
In MiB; `0` = no bound of its own. Not `0` together with
`host_max_frame_mb`.

host_ping_interval_s.description: Seconds between the link's pings; `0` = none.

task_poll_interval_s.description:
