Seconds between two `tasks/get` of a task whose server suggests no
`pollInterval`; at least 1.

McpStatus.description:
One registered MCP server's connection state: `status` is `connecting` |
`ready` | `stopped` | `error`, `tool_count` the tools it offers, and
`detail` says why on an error, or that a stopped server was idle-reaped
and reconnects on next use.

name.description: The exposed (prefixed) name a model sees and a thread stores.

upstream_name.description: The server's own name for it, shown when a prefix hides it.

Measured.description: Where a threshold was measured: a set run, and what the cut gave there.

accuracy.description:
Of those, the share of the labelled ones answered correctly. A cut
with no labelled item at or above it is not written (409
`no_labels`).

batch_id.description: The set run it was measured on.

coverage.description: The share of the run's answered items at or above the threshold.

labelled.description: How many labelled items the accuracy is over: at least 1.

MergeOutcome.description: One outcome an extra can have when assembled.

oneOf.description:
Its head was already an ancestor of `HEAD`, or the merge's diff
against its first parent was empty.
Skipped on the forge's word (`merged_at` set).

No shared history with the assembled `HEAD`: applied as a squash of
its changes since its fork point instead of a merge.
Only in a check-merge step or a failed run — assemble stops here.

Message.description: One stored message of a thread.

answered_by.description:
The alias that actually answered, when it was not `model` (a
fallback); `null` when `model` itself answered.

attachments.description: The files sent with this message.

context.description: The retrieval that ran for this user message; `null` when none ran.

created_at.description: When the message was written (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`).

images_note.description:
For a reply that a fallback without sight answered: who, for which
model, and what went to it in the images' place. Absent otherwise.

ir_messages.description:
An agentic turn's tool calls and results as JSON text; `null` for a
plain chat turn.

kb_refs.description: Knowledge bases picked with `#` for this user message only.

model.description:
A reply's model: the alias its turn asked for. `null` on user
messages and on replies saved before it was recorded.

pending_approvals.description:
The calls a gated turn's reply still waits on
(`POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/approvals` decides them). Absent when
none wait.

reasoning.description: A reasoning model's thinking trace; empty otherwise.

task.description:
On a late MCP task result (role `tool`): the task's facts. Absent
otherwise.

voice.description: How the turn was spoken; `null` for a typed turn.

MessageAck.description: A write that reports what it did in a sentence: `{"ok": true, "message": …}`.

message.description: What was done, for a person to read.

ok.description: Always `true`; a failure is an error answer instead.

MessageContext.description:
The retrieval that ran for one user message. Excerpt `n` in the
`<context>` block (and `[n]` in the answer) is `excerpts[n - 1]`.

budget_tokens.description: The budget the retrieval ran with.

dropped.description: Excerpts that ranked but did not fit the budget.

kb_ids.description:
The bases asked for: the thread's and the message's, as they were
then.

notes.description: Why something was not searched, or not fully: one sentence each.

searched.description: The bases that were searched, by name.

tokens.description: Tokens the excerpts use, heading paths included.

MessageTask.description: What a result row says of its task: `task` on a message of role `tool`.

ended_by.description:
Who cancelled it, for a cancel lmgw sent ("the dashboard", "device
'phone'"); `null` otherwise.

server_label.description: The label the tool was offered under when it was called.

status.description:
How it ended: `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, or `abandoned`
(the server no longer knows it, or its server row was removed).

structured_content.description:
The result's MCP `structuredContent`, for a view of the call
(client-apps design §7.5): the model reads the result's `content`,
and this only when the content was empty. Absent when the result
had none, and for a result stored by an earlier lmgw.

task_id.description: The server's id of the task.

MessageVoice.description:
How a turn was spoken, on its message: `null` on the message for a typed
turn. On a user message: how it was dictated or spoken in realtime mode,
the speech-to-text alias that was asked and the one that answered, and
the audio's length. On a spoken reply: the text-to-speech alias, the
voice, the part that was never heard and the turn's timing.

input.description:
On a user message: `audio` when the chat model heard the turn;
absent on the transcript path.

transcript_error.description: On a user message the model heard: why its transcription failed.

unheard.description:
The reply's text after the heard part, shown behind a "not heard"
marker. Not in `content`, so the model never sees it.

MetricDelta.description: One headline metric of a comparison.

band_pct.description: max(threshold, noise): the band a delta has to leave.

noise_pct.description: The larger relative spread of the two points, in percent.

note.description:
E.g. the two runs measured different prompt lengths (the verdict is
then `not_same_point`).

old.description: The previous run's value (median), and this run's.

stream_predict.description:
Their `n_predict`: as much as the slot holds, so none runs out before
the injected prompt's first token.

MixedResult.description:
The mixed phase: what an arriving long prompt costs streams that
are already decoding.

before_tok_s.description:
Per repetition: the median over the streams of each one's rate in the
steady window before the injection.

during_tok_s.description:
Per repetition: the median over the streams of each one's rate from
the injection to the injected request's first token.

notes.description:
Anything that makes a repetition's numbers partial (a stream that
ended before the injected first token, …).

solo_ttft_ms.description:
The prefill phase's median TTFT at the same prompt length, when it
measured that length.

stall_ms.description:
Per repetition: the longest inter-token gap of any stream across that
window — the stall.

ModelById.description: The OpenAiModel shape unless the caller sent anthropic-version, in which case AnthropicModel. No lmgw block on the single-model route.

ModelCapabilities.description:
The `capabilities` object of one model on `GET /v1/models`.

`task`, `endpoints` and `source` are always present — they are what makes
the entry actionable at all ("this id exists, here is where to send it,
here is how much to trust the rest"). Everything else is absent unless a
source stated it.

endpoints.description: The lmgw routes that accept this model id.

output_modalities.description:
The same vocabulary, plus `decisions`: what a decision model answers
with (llama.cpp's and OpenRouter's word). A client that checks
llama.cpp's `architecture.output_modalities` for `decisions` reads
this list instead. Absent = unknown.

source.description:
Where the facts came from: `gguf+config`, `catalog`, `config`, or
`owner` (an alias's capabilities override).

speech.description:
A text-to-speech model's expressive controls — what `instructions`,
inline tags, `language` and `stream_format` do on it
(the speech capabilities object). A local audio model's is derived; a
cloud alias has one only through an alias's capabilities override.

task.description:
`chat` | `embedding` | `rerank` | `decision` (a decision model,
answering on `/v1/systemone`) | `tts` | `asr` | an audio.cpp task
name | an image task | `realtime` (an OpenAI Realtime model, no lmgw
route). Determines `endpoints`.

vision.description:
`input_modalities` contains `image`. Redundant with the list on
purpose: a client can read this one boolean to decide whether to
send images, e.g. whether a session gets a screenshot tool. Absent
exactly when `input_modalities` is absent.

ModelCheck.description:
One model's pre-flight result; `class` says which kind of model it is and
so which fields it has.

oneOf.description: A chat-class model.

advisories.description: The model starts, but misbehaves under some input.

ok.description: No problems. Advisories do not count.

problems.description: Why the model cannot load as configured.

oneOf.description: An embedding, rerank or decision model.

kind.description: `embed`, `rerank` or `decision`.

oneOf.description: An image-generation model.

applied.description: `apply` only: whether the configuration was applied.

held.description: `apply` only: the GPU hold kept the container from starting again.

ok.description:
False when the model was still serving requests and was left
running, or could not be stopped under the hold.

port.description: The port, when the action left the container up.

running.description: `apply` only: whether the container is running afterwards.

ModelIdentity.description: The model the run measured, filled in by the benchmark runner.

quant.description: From the GGUF header's file type.

ModelLicence.description:
The licence a GGUF header states (`general.license`, with the optional
`general.license.name` and `general.license.link`). Information only: it
is never a filter, a ranking or a warning. At least one field is set.

id.description:
`general.license`: an SPDX-like id or a name, such as `apache-2.0`
or `other`.

name.description: `general.license.name`.

ModelList.description: OpenAiModelList unless the caller sent anthropic-version, in which case AnthropicModelList.

endpoints.description: Every path listed here exists in this API and carries the capability its own operation documents.
Every path listed here exists in this API and carries the capability its own operation documents.

tail.description: How many lines were asked for.

enabled.description: Null when no model with this id is configured.

engine.description: The engine the class runs: `llama-server`, `audio.cpp` or `sd-server`.

image.description: The container image in effect.

runtime.description: The running container, or null when nothing has started this model.

ModelTestFailed.description: A chat, aux or image model that did not load or did not answer.

container_log.description: The lines of the model's container log that look like the reason.

endpoint.description: For an image model: the route the probe went to.

error.description: What went wrong.

ok.description: Always `false`.

public_name.description: For an image model: the name clients call it by.

ModelTestPassed.description:
An aux model that loaded and answered its probe; the first part of a
chat model's pass.

answer.description:
For `decide`: the model's answer to the probe's `choice` question, as
it gave it. The test does not judge the choice, only that the route
answered with one of the options and probabilities that sum to 1
(decision-models design §3.7).

class.description:
`aux` for an aux model's pass, `chat` where this is the first part of
a chat model's.

input_tokens.description: For `decide`: the input tokens the server reported for the question.

latency_ms.description: How long the load and the probe took, in milliseconds.

ok.description: Always `true`.

probe.description:
What was sent: `generate` (one token), `embed`, `rerank` or `decide`
(one System One `choice` question on `/v1/systemone`).

scored.description: For `rerank`: how many documents came back scored.

fence.description:
Domains a fetch may touch. Empty derives the fence from the root's own
host, which is the safe default rather than "anywhere".

kind.description: `llms_txt` | `markdown` | `rustdoc_json` | `html`.

criteria.description: What a yes and a no mean, when the question alone does not say.

instructions.description: The yes/no question: a string, an object or an array.

OngoingInput.description:
`ongoing` in a folder create or patch: an object marks the folder as one
ongoing conversation (its defaults must name a model), `null` ends that.

idle_minutes.description:
Minutes without a message after which a new thread starts; `0`: only
when a client asks. A whole number of zero or more.

code.description: lmgw's own machine-readable error code (e.g. gpu_hold, gpu_benchmark), not the HTTP status.

param.description: Always null: lmgw does not attribute an error to one request field.

type.description: e.g. invalid_request_error, authentication_error, not_found_error, rate_limit_error, api_error.

created.description: Stable for the life of the gateway process rather than the time of each request; the catalog's own timestamp when it has one.

prompt.description: USD per prompt token, as a decimal string; "0" for a local model.

OpenLink.description: One open connection of a device.

call.description:
A voice link that is a WebRTC call (`POST /v1/realtime/calls`): the
call's id, as the status block's `webrtc.calls` lists it; `null` for
a WebSocket session and for the other kinds.

keepalive_s.description:
The keep-alive it asked for, in seconds: a feed's `keepalive_s`;
`null` for the other kinds.

peer.description:
The address it connected from (IP and port); `null` when lmgw did
not see one.

OpenLinks.description: How many connections of one kind a device holds open.

kind.description: `feed`, `voice` or `tools`.

links.description:
Each of them, the oldest first (device link design §9.3): "feed
(keep-alive 120 s, since 09:00, from 192.0.2.2)".

description.description: What the option means; blank sends `null`.
What the option means; blank sends `null`.

OptionProbability.description: One option of a `DecideAnswer` and its probability.

role_guess.description:
`weights | mmproj | drafter | imatrix`, guessed from the filename.
Only weights can be wired up as a model; the rest are companions a
model's editor attaches (or leftovers). Empty from an older gateway.

suggested_id.description: Model id the create flow proposes for it.

PairingTokenView.description: A device's latest pairing token: when it lapses, and what became of it.

alive.description:
Whether it is alive now: not lapsed, not ended. A used token stays
alive until then, for its own key's repeat.

created_at.description: When it was minted and when it lapses, RFC 3339 UTC.

ended_at.description: When the owner ended it (closing the QR card, a new token).

used_at.description: When it was used, and from which address.

min_p.description: llama.cpp `min_p`; only the OpenAI egress emits it.

repeat_penalty.description: llama.cpp `repeat_penalty`; only the OpenAI egress emits it.

hidden.description:
Bare (unprefixed) model ids hidden from `/v1/models` and the client
catalog for this upstream — still reachable directly by name, just
not advertised. `POST /api/op/model_visibility` toggles membership.

PcmFormat.description:
The PCM a streamed answer carries, as the page assembles it into a WAV:
the stream itself states none of it. The strings the inputs hold.

PcmFormatInput.description:
The PCM a streamed answer carries, as the page assembles it into a WAV:
the stream itself states none of it. The strings the inputs hold.

Phase.description: One phase of a run, in suite order.

oneOf.description: `podman run` to a healthy server (the integration's, not the engine's).

PhaseError.description: A phase that ended with an error. The points measured before it are kept.

PhaseSpan.description: A phase's band on the timeline.

end_ms.description: `None` while the phase is still running.

PlanChange.description: One field a plan would change on a configured row.

current.description: The row's value now; null when unset.

why.description: The plan's reason for the planned value; null when it gives none.

PlanUnset.description: One setting a plan would clear on a configured chat row.

PlannedProbe.description: A probe the plan would run, or why it would not.

skip.description:
`None`: it runs. Judged on the row's capabilities; the live server's
`chat_template_caps` may still skip `tool_call` at run time.

PlayoutSource.description: Where a call's playout allowance comes from (calls design §5.3).

oneOf.description:
The client's latest playout report (`lmgw.output_audio.playout`): the
measured playout delay less half the round trip.

One frame plus twice the client's interarrival jitter: before the
first report, on an unbound call, and after reports stopped.
One frame: no receiver report yet.

PointPlan.description:
The points a run measures, derived from the live server's per-slot
context and slot count — or, in `bench_plan`, provisionally from the row's
own numbers.

concurrent.description: Stream counts *N*, ascending; the last one is *N_slots*.

decode.description: Context depths *D*, ascending; the last one is *D_max* = *S* − *G* − 1.

mixed.description:
`None` when the server has a single slot, or its context cannot hold
a decoding stream.

needle_tokens.description:
The needle probe's prompt length, *P_max* − 512; `None` when the
context is too small to hold one.

notes.description: Why a phase has fewer points than usual, or none at all.

prefill.description: Prompt lengths *P*, ascending; the last one is *P_max* = *S* − 2.

provisional.description:
True when derived from the row's configuration rather than read from a
running server (`bench_plan`).

energy.description: Over the TTFT windows; tokens are the evaluated prompt tokens.

energy_unmeasured.description:
Why `energy` is `None` although the card reports power: a window
shorter than the GPU sampler resolves (two of its ticks, 200 ms at
the 100 ms tick), whose figure would have been the
ticks' average power times its length rather than a measurement.
`None` otherwise.

evaluated_tokens.description:
`timings.prompt_n`: what the server actually evaluated. Equal to *P*
when the KV cache stayed out of it.

ttft_ms.description: Client-side: request sent → first streamed token.

PreviewTokens.description: The token counts of a preview, through the universal counter.

answered_by.description: The alias that counted, when it was not `alias` (a fallback).

approx.description:
How the counts are approximate, as `x-lmgw-count-approximate` says
it; empty when they are exact.

price.description:
The rate of a unit other than tokens, per that unit's scale (per
minute of input audio, per 1M input characters, per generated image,
per answered request). `None` on a `per_mtok` row, whose rates are the
four above; those four are `None` on every other row.

ProbeChange.description: One probe's outcome in both runs.

verdict.description:
A pass that became a fail or an error is a regression; the reverse an
improvement.

body.description:
The raw body when it is not a chat completion: an error status's body,
`/apply-template`'s rendered prompt.

status.description: The HTTP status; `None` when the request never got one.

oneOf.description: Always last: it is the one probe with a full-context prefill.
An observation, not a verdict (`reasoning_history`).
Not applicable to this model; `detail` says why.
The server answered with an error status, or not at all.

ProbeReport.description: The probe results stored with a run.

detail.description: One line: what passed or failed, the skip reason, or the error.

evidence.description:
The responses judged — one, or four for `deterministic` (the cached
pair, then the no-cache pair).

builtin.description:
The built-in profile this row is (`concise`); `null` for one of the
owner's own. Read only.

follows_builtin.description:
The fields a built-in row takes from the built-in text, so they
follow its improvements. Read only.

length_rule.description: How long replies are; empty for none.

name.description: Unique in any case; never `default`.

persona.description:
Who the model is and how it sounds; empty for none. When set, it
takes the thread's system prompt's place.

voice_block.description:
The voice turn's block: `null` for the generic one, `""` for none, a
text to use as it is.

ProfileChoice.description:
`chat_profile` as a settings patch writes it (design §3.3): a profile
id, as a number or as a numeric text, or `""` for none.

ProfileDraft.description:
A profile's content fields, with nothing saved: what Preview, Test and
Speak take, and what a create fills in.

ProfileVoice.description:
The speech part of a profile: the subset of a thread's voice settings a
profile carries, with the same checks and meanings. Each `null` inherits.

speech_style.description:
The speaking style the text-to-speech model is given; an empty text
is none.

voice.description:
A voice of that text-to-speech model, or of the Chat's own when
`tts_alias` is `null`.

ProfileVoiceInput.description:
The speech part of a profile: the subset of a thread's voice settings a
profile carries, with the same checks and meanings. Each `null` inherits.

speech_style.description:
The speaking style the text-to-speech model is given; an empty text
is none.

voice.description:
A voice of that text-to-speech model, or of the Chat's own when
`tts_alias` is `null`.

QuestionDraft.description: One question as the form holds it.

id.description: The key the answer comes back under.

QuestionDraftInput.description: One question as the form holds it.

id.description: The key the answer comes back under.

accuracy.description:
The share of `scored` answered correctly: the winner (`choice`),
P(yes) ≥ 0.5 (`noul`), the nearest level (`score`) equal to the
label; `null` when nothing is scored.

answered.description: Items whose run answered this question.

classes.description:
The classes in matrix order, spelled as labels are kept: the options'
names, the levels' indices from `"0"`, or `yes` and `no`.

confusion.description: Rows the labels, columns the predictions, both in `classes` order.

curve.description:
One point per distinct confidence (`choice`, `score`) or certainty,
max(p, 1 − p) (`noul`), lowest first.

labelled.description: Items with an expected answer for this question.

mae.description:
`score` only: the mean absolute distance, in levels, between the
expected level (the fractional `score`) and the label.

reliability.description:
The non-empty ones of `bins` equal-width bins over the predicted
probability, lowest first: the winner's (`choice`), the nearest
level's (`score`), P(yes) (`noul`). Labelled answers only.

scored.description: Items both answered and labelled: what `accuracy` is over.

unreadable.description:
Items whose run is a 2xx without a readable answer to this question
(none of its type, a winner the question does not offer, the nearest
level's probability missing).

default_model.description: The model loading the set picks; blank picks none.

thresholds.description: Per question id; a question with none has 0, not measured.

default_model.description: The model loading the set picks; blank picks none.

thresholds.description: Per question id; a question with none has 0, not measured.

option_span.description: A `choice` question's options alone; `null` for the other types.

tokens.description: Its instructions and its options, levels or criteria.

RateLimit.description:
The forge API's remaining quota. Without a token GitHub allows 60 requests
an hour; when the limit is hit, the extras picker shows the reset time
instead of an empty list.

RealtimeAvailability.description: Whether voice mode may bind the thread.

admin_tools.description:
The thread carries lmgw's admin tools while the self-admin level is
`full`: its tools can change lmgw. Shown, never a refusal.

code.description:
The refusal's code, the one the bind answers with
(`chat_thread_admin`); `null` when `ok`.

RealtimeBudgetStage.description: One stage of the cascade and what it is expected to hold on the GPU.

alias.description:
The alias the stage runs on; `None` for turn detection and for a
stage nothing is configured for.

bytes.description:
The expected footprint; `None` = unknown, and the total is then a
lower bound.

model.description: The local model, as `<class>/<model id>`.

note.description: Where the figure comes from, or why there is none.

placement.description:
`local` (a model lmgw runs on this GPU) | `cloud` | `external` (a
server lmgw does not manage) | `cpu` | `shared` (the same local model
as an earlier stage, counted once) | `unset` | `unresolved`.

RealtimeSettings.description:
The realtime settings, with `default_instructions` spelled
out the way the Chat's default system prompt is: the text in force, the
built-in text beside it, and whether the setting is unset.

asr_alias.description:
The speech-to-text alias turns are transcribed with; empty =
the Chat's transcription model.

barge_in_check_alias.description: Empty = the session's own ASR alias.

barge_in_check_scripts.description: Unicode script names; empty = every script.

default_instructions.description:
The instructions a session with audio output uses while the client
gives none: the configured text, `""` for none, or the built-in text
while the setting is unset.

default_instructions_builtin.description:
The built-in voice-assistant prompt — what saving
`default_instructions` as this text returns to.

default_instructions_is_builtin.description:
The setting is unset, so it follows the built-in text across
releases.

default_model.description: The chat alias a session starts on; empty = none.

default_voice.description:
The voice a session speaks with when it names none or an OpenAI
built-in voice; empty = the TTS row's default preset.

echo_tail_ms.description:
The barge-in margin's tail on top of the round trip, in ms: the round
trip from pings on a WebSocket, from RTCP receiver reports on a
WebRTC call.

max_frame_mb.description:
In MiB; `0` = bounded by the message limit (not both). WebSocket
only: a WebRTC call's single message is bounded by its stack, 256 KiB.

max_message_mb.description:
In MiB; `0` = no bound (not both). The largest WebSocket message; on
a WebRTC call also the largest event lmgw sends in one message and
what may wait for the call's session.

model_map.description: Client model names mapped to lmgw aliases.

output_lead_ms.description:
How far a WebSocket session's audio runs ahead of real time, in ms;
not used on a WebRTC call, whose frame clock sends in real time.

ping_interval_s.description:
`0` = no pings and no liveness bound at all. On a WebRTC call also how
long it may stay silent, take to connect and open its events channel,
or wait on a held thread, how long a closing call waits for its last
event's delivery, and when playout reports count as stopped.

tag_hint.description:
An audio response's prompt says what square brackets do for the TTS:
the sounds it can make, or the delivery cues it takes.

tts_alias.description:
The text-to-speech alias a session speaks with; empty = none.
Its task is `tts` or `vdes`.

voice_map.description: Client voice names mapped to voices of the TTS model.

webrtc_commit_window_ms.description:
How far past its stamp a push-to-talk commit on a WebRTC call takes
frames, and how long it waits for them, in ms. Applies to the next
call.

webrtc_enabled.description:
The UDP listener for WebRTC calls, beside the HTTP listener and
beside the device listener (its sockets follow that one's addresses
and port); applies at the next start.

webrtc_output_kbps.description:
A WebRTC call's Opus output bitrate in kbps, capped by the phone's
`maxaveragebitrate`. Applies to the next call.

webrtc_port.description:
The UDP port WebRTC calls use beside the HTTP listener: `null` =
the HTTP port's number, `0` = chosen by the OS. Calls over a paired
device's listener use that listener's port instead. Applies at the
next start.

webrtc_reorder_ms.description:
How long a WebRTC call's frame waits for a missing earlier one, in
ms; `0` = no wait. Applies to the next call.

RealtimeSettingsPatch.description:
Sparse patch over `RealtimeSettings`: a field left out keeps its value.
The two maps and the two lists are replaced whole, like a class's
`extra_run_args`.

asr_alias.description:
The speech-to-text alias turns are transcribed with; `""` = the
Chat's transcription model. Must be an alias whose task is `asr`.

barge_in_check_alias.description:
The ASR alias the word check transcribes with; `""` = the session's
own ASR alias. Must be an alias whose task is `asr`.

barge_in_check_scripts.description:
Unicode script names (Latin, Cyrillic, Han, …); `[]` = every script.
Replaces the whole list.

default_instructions.description:
The instructions a session with audio output uses while the client
gives none. The built-in text returns to the built-in default (and
follows it from then on); `""` = none.

default_model.description:
The chat alias a session starts on when the client names none, or
names an OpenAI Realtime model; `""` = none. Must be a chat alias.

default_voice.description:
The voice a session speaks with when it names none, or names an
OpenAI built-in voice; `""` = the TTS row's default preset.

longest_pause_ms.description:
The longest silence in synthesized speech, in ms; `0` = keep the
engine's silences.

max_frame_mb.description: In MiB; `0` = bounded by `max_message_mb`. Not `0` together with it.

max_message_mb.description:
In MiB; `0` = no bound. Not `0` together with `max_frame_mb`. The
largest WebSocket message a client sends; on a WebRTC call also the
largest event lmgw sends in one message and what may wait for the
call's session before the call ends.

model_map.description:
Client model names mapped to lmgw aliases — `session.model` to a chat
alias, a transcription model to an ASR alias. Replaces the whole map.

ping_interval_s.description: `0` = no pings, and no liveness bound at all.

semantic_vad.description:
The Smart Turn rows by eagerness; a row or field left out keeps its
value.

speech_instructions.description:
The speech instructions a session's TTS gets while the client sends
none: a speaking style, or a voice-design row's description. `""` =
none.

tag_hint.description: Whether an audio response's prompt names the sounds the TTS can make.

threshold.description:
`server_vad.threshold`: the speech probability that counts as voice,
`0.0..=1.0`.

tts_alias.description:
The text-to-speech alias a session speaks with; `""` = none. Must be
an alias whose task is `tts`, or `vdes` (a voice designed from the
speech instructions).

voice_map.description:
Client voice names mapped to voices of the TTS model. Replaces the
whole map.

webrtc_commit_window_ms.description:
How far past its own stamp a push-to-talk commit on a WebRTC call
takes frames, and how long it waits for them, in ms. Applies to the
next call.

webrtc_enabled.description:
The UDP listener for WebRTC calls (`POST /v1/realtime/calls`),
beside the HTTP listener and beside the device listener, whose
addresses and port its sockets follow; off, a call on either is
refused 503. Applies at the next start.

webrtc_output_kbps.description:
A WebRTC call's Opus output bitrate in kbps, 6 to 510, capped by the
phone's maxaveragebitrate. Applies to the next call.

webrtc_port.description:
The UDP port WebRTC calls use beside the HTTP listener: `null` = the
HTTP port's number, `0` = chosen by the OS, else 1 to 65535. Calls
over a paired device's listener use that listener's port instead.
Applies at the next start.

webrtc_reorder_ms.description:
How long a WebRTC call's frame waits for a missing earlier one, in
ms; `0` = no wait, the gap concealed at once. At most 40 950 (what
str0m can hold behind a gap). Applies to the next call.

Reasoning.description:
A profile's reasoning switch; `null` where it is used inherits (the
thread's own fields win over it, the route's default comes after it).

ReasoningCaps.description: Reasoning / thinking support and how a request controls it.

budget_tokens.description:
The configured default thinking-token budget, when set and non-zero
(a zero budget is published as `enabled: false`, not as a budget).

can_disable.description: Whether a request can switch thinking off entirely.

control.description:
The exact header and body fields that work on this route; omitted when
empty (nothing to control on a `fixed` model).

default.description: The effort in force when the request sets none.

enabled.description:
The default state as this alias is configured. Absent when no source
states it — "the catalog says the model supports reasoning" does not
say whether it is on.

kind.description:
`fixed` (nothing to change per request), `toggle` (on/off per
request), `levels` (effort selectable per request).

levels.description:
Accepted effort values, least → most in the canonical order. Only for
`kind == "levels"`; omitted entirely when empty.

preserve_history.description: Whether replayed reasoning of earlier turns reaches the model again.

ReasoningControl.description: Per-request reasoning control: on/off, effort level, thinking-token budget.

RefEntry.description: One branch or tag as `git ls-remote` reports it.

RegistryUpdate.description:
A registry image's update state: the digest the registry serves for
the tag now, against the digests podman recorded when the image was
pulled. Checked anonymously (the registry's bearer-token flow), by the same
schedule and **Check now** as the builds.

A multi-arch tag is an index: the registry answers with the index digest,
and podman's `RepoDigests` for such a pull normally carries it too. When it
carries only the platform manifest's digest instead, the index is read and
its members compared, so that case is not mistaken for an update.

error.description:
Why the comparison could not be made: the registry did not answer, it
wants credentials, it rate-limited the check, or podman recorded no
digest to compare with (an image built or loaded here, not pulled).

local_digests.description:
The `sha256:…` digests podman recorded for this repository on the
local image, right now.

reference.description:
The fully qualified reference that was checked
(`ghcr.io/0xshug0/audio.cpp:full-cuda12`) — what **Pull update**
(`container_image_pull`) pulls.

remote_digest.description:
`sha256:…` the registry serves for the tag; `None` when it could not
be asked (see `error`).

update_available.description: The registry serves something the local image is not.

ReliabilityBin.description:
One reliability bin that holds an answer: the labelled answers whose
predicted probability falls in `[lower, upper)` (the last bin includes
1). `lower` is `index / bins` and `upper` `(index + 1) / bins`, the very
values an answer is placed by. A bin the list skips holds none.

observed.description:
The observed rate of what was predicted: the share whose winner
(`choice`) or nearest level (`score`) is the label; for `noul`, the
share labelled yes (the bins sort by P(yes)).

parts.description: >1 = split GGUF; selecting it downloads all parts.

role.description:
Filename heuristic, in the vocabulary of the target that was listed:
`weights | mmproj | drafter | other` for chat/aux/audio, and
`diffusion | checkpoint | vae | text_encoder | lora | upscaler | other`
for `image`. A string, not an enum, on
both sides of the wire — the image roles are guesses the editor lets
the user override, and a new one must not break an old client.

RepoPreset.description:
One entry of the build editor's repository picker: a preset source repository for a
build.

default_ref.description: The default branch — what a new build's `ref` starts as.

RequestRow.description:
One request's summary — the `request` SSE frame and the
row shape of `GET /api/logs` (log rows additionally carry `mcp_tool` and
`pricing`).

audio_in_ms.description:
What the request processed besides tokens, each only when it was
measured or the provider reported it: input audio in milliseconds,
input characters as sent, generated images. `None` = not measured,
which is not the same as zero — render a dash.

cached_in_tokens.description:
The cache subsets of `prompt_tokens`, when the provider reported them —
without these a row that cost 8x its neighbour looks identical to it.
`None` = the provider said nothing, which is not the same as zero.

client_key.description:
Name of the gateway API key that made the call (never the key itself);
absent when auth is disabled or the call was made in-process.

cost_micro.description:
Currency micro-units. `None` = **unpriced**, which is not the same as
free — render a dash, never a 0.

degraded.description:
What the request's content lost on its way to a model that lacks a
capability: "fallback 'x' lacks vision: 3 images sent as
placeholders", "'m' lacks audio: transcript sent", several joined by
"; ". `None` = nothing was degraded.

fallback_reason.description:
Why a fallback answered instead of the requested local model: `hold`
(the GPU hold), `external_vram` (VRAM outside lmgw's control was
short), `background` (a background candidate alias), `unavailable`
(a candidate alias with no model it may use). `None` = no
fallback; the fallback itself is `upstream_name` / `upstream_model`.

key_id.description:
`api_keys.id` behind `client_key` — the id is what a key filter matches
on, and a name match breaks the moment a key is renamed.

max_tokens_clamped.description:
`max_tokens` lmgw lowered a client-set value to, on a ladder rung or a
guarded unified-KV pool. `None` = not clamped — either the row is unguarded, or the
client's value already fit.

mcp_tool.description: MCP tool name for `ingress_proto = "mcp"` rows; absent on SSE frames.

pricing.description:
How the row was priced: the rates it recorded when it was written,
so each priced part can be shown as quantity × rate even after the
price has changed. On `GET /api/logs` rows only; absent on SSE
frames, which carry the cost and the quantities alone.

prompt_tokens.description: **Total** input for the call, cache included.

rung.description:
The rung a ladder row answered from — or, for a refusal, the rung it
was judged on — 1-based. `None` for a row without
a ladder, and for a request its fallback answered.

texts.description: TEI's spelling — either works; an embedding-only row is refused.

RerankResponse.description: Jina's results shape, regardless of which request spelling was sent. Built by lmgw from the model's scores, never relayed: no result carries its document.

model.description: The model as the request named it.

index.description: The document's position in the request.

prompt_tokens.description: What the model reported; 0 when it reported nothing.

total_tokens.description: The same number: reranking generates nothing.

ResolvedExtra.description: One extra with the commit it resolved to for a run.

sha.description: Full commit SHA that was (or will be) merged.

ResolvedInputs.description:
What every "auto" and every "follow the head" of a build became for one
run. Filled by the run executor; the config hash is computed
over these values, never over the unresolved definition.

arch.description: The arch list passed to the build, in the order passed.

base_sha.description: Full SHA the base ref resolved to.

edits.description:
The edits applied — the build's explicit list, or the preset's for
`dockerfile`.

extras.description:
The extras the run merges, in order, each with its resolved SHA. A
`pr` extra already merged upstream is skipped by the run and left out
here — it does not change the image.

Response.description: An upstream that speaks the Responses API natively is relayed as it sends the body: such a body may carry status queued (background), a null or missing usage and no store. lmgw's own translation always sends usage and store.

store.description: Whether lmgw stored this response, so a later request can continue from it with previous_response_id. Sent by lmgw's own translation; a verbatim upstream body may leave it out.

input_tokens_details.description: Tokens read from and written to the prompt cache, both part of input_tokens; 0 when the upstream reported none (cache_write_tokens is lmgw's own addition and absent from a verbatim upstream body).

outline.description: Output items at a glance, e.g. `2 mcp_call, message`.

type.description: response.created … response.completed/.incomplete/.failed, response.output_text.delta, the mcp_*/function_call_* tool-call events, …

input.description: A string (one user turn), or an array of items.

items.description: A message ({type:message,role,content}), a prior turn's {type:function_call,call_id,name,arguments} (call_id as lmgw gave it: a Gemini model's carries its thought signature and runs to hundreds of characters; echo it exactly, and do not send it to another provider directly) or {type:function_call_output,call_id,output} (output a string, or an array of {type:input_text,text} and {type:input_image,image_url} items: a base64 data: image goes on as an image where the upstream's tool results take one and as a named placeholder elsewhere, another URL as a resource naming it, and any other item as its JSON text), an mcp_call echo, or an {type:mcp_approval_response,approval_request_id,approve,reason} verdict on a previous response's pending call.

instructions.description: Becomes the leading system message; an explicit empty string drops it on a chained call.

metadata.description: Echoed back verbatim on the response object.

previous_response_id.description: Continues a stored response: its conversation, tool calls and results included, goes ahead of this call's input, and mcp_approval_response items settle the calls it stopped at. 400 while the gateway's response store is switched off; 404 when no stored response has this id (it was evicted, or created with storing off).

reasoning.description: The one reasoning control this dialect reads: reasoning.effort.

store.description: Whether lmgw keeps this response, so a later call can continue it with previous_response_id (default true). Storing also needs the gateway's response store, which is on by default: a request can turn storing off, never on. The response object's store says whether this response was kept, so a client can see up front whether previous_response_id will work. On an upstream that implements the Responses API itself the body goes there as sent, and storing is the provider's.

text.description: text.format is translated to the chat-completions response_format (json_schema/json_object) for OpenAI-protocol upstreams.

tools.description: function tools the loop hands back to the client; mcp tools run server-side on lmgw's own registered MCP servers. Hosted tools (web_search, file_search, code_interpreter, image_generation, computer_use) are refused.

allowed_tools.description: Tool names, as a list or {tool_names}; a name matches the exposed or the server's own spelling (docs__query or query). An empty list leaves nothing. read_only is refused: lmgw does not read MCP tool annotations.

require_approval.description: "never" (default) | "always" | {never:{tool_names}, always:{tool_names}}. read_only is refused, as in allowed_tools.

server_label.description: Matches a registered MCP server's own tool prefix (or its name when it has none) — lmgw resolves this against its own servers, never against a client-supplied server_url.

truncation.description: Refused when "auto": lmgw never silently drops conversation history.

ResultTask.description: The MCP task a call started, on its `result` frame.

task_id.description: The server's id of the task.

RetriedRequest.description:
A request the engine sent a second time because its connection broke
before any response arrived. What the
step recorded is the second attempt's.

error.description: Why the first attempt failed, with its whole cause chain.

stage.description:
The step it belonged to, as the progress line named it
("prefill: 32768 tokens, repetition 1/3").

RevokeKind.description:
What revoked a key, as a `CLOSE_REVOKED` close's reason starts with it
and the change feed's `revoked` event carries it (`kind`):

- `device_disabled`: a paired device was disabled; it may be enabled
  again, so it keeps its pairing;
- `key_expired`: a paired device's key passed its expiry;
- `key_unknown`: a paired device's key was rotated or deleted: pair the
  device again;
- `certificate_expired`: a paired device's client certificate passed its
  `notAfter` while the connection was open (device link design §5.1):
  pair the device again;
- `revoked`: any other kind of key, for any of these.

Forward compatible like every enum a client reads: a token a newer
gateway sends reads as `RevokeKind::Unknown`, as sent. One an older
gateway does not send at all — a close reason without a token, a
`revoked` event without `kind` — is an empty `Unknown`, the default, so
a client never reads a device's rotation as another key's revocation.

RouterSettings.description:
The chat/aux *class* settings.
`container_name`/`listen_port`/`models_max`/
`auto_start` left with router mode: names are derived, ports are dynamic,
and auto-start is the per-model `warm_start` flag.

extra_run_args.description: Class default; a model's own `extra_run_args` overrides it.

image.description: Class default; a model's own `image` overrides it.

request_timeout_seconds.description:
Per-request ceiling for the class, in seconds. **0 = the maximum
possible** — no deadline of lmgw's own. One per class since the four
stopped sharing a single 600 s constant.

Row.description:
One row of the review table.

Both a live frame and a stored result use this shape, so the table renders
the same whether the run is in flight or was finished last week.

attention.description:
The output equals the fallback, or the call failed; through a question
set also a confidence below the set's measured threshold (`decide`).

columns.description:
The manifest's `columns`, rendered. Order comes from the manifest, not
from this map.

id.description:
`item.id` rendered. Empty marks the row errored — there is no
stable identity to apply anything against.

item.description:
The **source** item, kept so a re-run can re-fetch and re-classify this
row without re-listing the mailbox. Not shown anywhere.

output.description: The structured answer. `null` for a list-only run, which makes no call.

prompt.description:
Exactly the `user` text the model received, for the details modal.
Kept per row because "why did it say that" is the question the
review table exists to answer.

raw.description: What the model actually replied, so a surprising answer is explainable.

set.description:
The question set that classified this row, as the run read it
(`decide`); `None` for the model call. "Save as labelled set" saves
a run's rows into the set stamped on them.

RowPricing.description:
The rates a request row was priced with and its cost's parts, each as
the row snapshotted it. `None` = that part or rate did not apply, or
(for the costs) was unknown — never 0.

cost_in_micro.description:
The cost's token parts and its part in every other unit, in currency
micro-units.

currency.description: The gateway's configured currency, which every amount here is in.

in_remainder.description:
Whether this row is counted in the unpriced remainder the usage
totals state beside their cost (`cost_unknown_requests`): its cost is
unknown, it is no tool call, and it was answered or spent something
(tokens or a measured quantity). `false` for a priced row, a tool
call, and a refusal or failure that spent nothing: nothing billed is
missing from a total.

price_per_audio_minute.description:
The other units' rates: per minute of input audio, per 1M input
characters, per generated image, per answered request.

RunResults.description: Everything a run measured apart from the probes and the timeline.

complete.description:
True once every selected phase finished without an error. A crash, a
cancel or a phase error leaves it false: the numbers present are real,
the set is partial.

corpus_tokens.description: The corpus, tokenized by the bench server.

phases_done.description: Phases that ran to the end, in order.

prompt_prefix.description:
The token ids every measured prompt starts with: the vocabulary's
BOS where it adds one — llama-server adds none to a token-id prompt —
counted inside each prompt's length. Empty when the
vocabulary adds nothing.

retried.description:
Requests sent a second time after a broken connection,
in the order they happened.

Rung.description:
One ladder rung above the base — its own weights and its own context. The base rung is
never one of these; it stays the row's own `gguf_path` and `ctx_size`.

Rung2.description:
One rung above the base: its own weights and its own `-c`.
`ctx_size` is a real token count: a rung with no context at all is not a
rung, so saving one with a non-positive value is refused.

ctx_size.description:
`--ctx-size` for this rung — the same meaning `ctx_size` has
everywhere else: it is `-c`, never the per-slot number.

gguf_path.description:
GGUF path relative to the models dir, exactly like the base row's
`gguf_path`.

RungDetail.description: One ladder rung as the model read shows it.

command_line.description: The `podman run …` command line this rung renders to.

of.description: How many rungs the ladder has.

per_slot_ctx.description:
The context one slot gets on this rung; null when the base row
predates the rule that derives it.

rung.description: This rung's number, from 1 (the base row).

switchover.description: The prompt length at which a request moves up to the next rung.

RungFootprint.description:
A model's estimated GPU cost. The CUDA context, allocator slack and a
projector's compute buffer are not in it; those are the headroom's.

compute_bytes.description:
The compute buffers llama.cpp reserves on the card, derived from the
header and the row's slots, batch sizes and context: for a chat row
(a ladder rung) its own context's and its MTP or draft context's,
summed.

ctx_tokens.description:
Context the KV figure was computed for; `None` when it could not be
derived (also why `kv_cache_bytes` would be 0).

kv_cache_bytes.description:
The KV cache, a speculative row's MTP or draft cache and recurrent
state included.

note.description: Why a term is missing or approximate, when it is.

RungStatus.description: The rung a container runs, 1-based (the base is rung 1).

error.description: Why the rung failed, when it did.

load_seconds.description: Seconds it took the rung to become ready.

rung.description: This rung's number, from 1 (the base row).

climbing.description: A climb in progress: to which rung, why, and what it is doing now.

draining_for_owner.description:
A foreground admission is waiting for room, and background traffic takes
no new work on this model until it is over. Absent = false.

image_capabilities.description:
What an image container reported about its loaded pipeline. `None` for
every other class, and for an image container whose capabilities route
answered anything but a 200.

llama_props.description:
What a llama-server container said about itself in `GET /props`.
`None` for every other engine, and when the
read failed — `warnings` then says why.

owner.description:
Whom the container runs for:
`"background"` when a background candidate alias started it and
foreground traffic has not claimed it since. `None` — absent from the
frame — is foreground: every request that is not a background candidate
alias's, every warm, boot or operator start, and lmgw's own in-process
callers. That is every container of an install without background
traffic.

placement.description:
`"cpu"` for an audio container started on the CPU (the per-row CPU
switch): no VRAM, not stopped by the GPU hold. `None` — absent from
the frame — is the GPU, every other container.

port.description: `0` while the entry is `starting` — no port has been allocated yet.

rung.description:
The rung this container runs. `None` for a row
without a ladder, and `#[serde(default)]` so a frame from before this
field existed still decodes.

sends.description:
Sends in flight as the ladder gate counts them — what a climb drains.
Only ladder sends are counted, so this is zero on every other row.

state.description: `starting | ready | stopping`.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal problems this model's start found.
Empty for a clean one, and absent from a frame older than the class.

Sampling.description:
The sampling every request of a run uses: pinned, so builds compare
and speculative decoding's acceptance does not wander with the row's own
sampler.

legend.description: Each level's index (`"0"`, `"1"`, …) with its description.

probabilities.description: Each level's index with its probability.

score.description:
The expected level index, weighted by probability: it can fall between
two levels.

ScoreLabels.description: How a `score` question's label column reads: every value one way.

oneOf.description: Each value is a level's exact text.
Each value is a level's index, from 0.

criteria.description: The levels' descriptions, lowest first: 2 to 10 of them.

instructions.description: The question: a string, an object or an array.

rerank_skipped.description:
The rerank stage ran but did not score this candidate: `score` is then
its RRF score and it ranks behind the reranked ones. Absent when false.

score.description:
The score the final order is by: the reranker's when it ran, RRF's
otherwise.

kind.description: `t` the title, `m` a message, `a` an attachment's name.

snippet.description:
The text around the match, with the match between U+E000 and U+E001
(private-use characters; escape the text before turning them into
markup).

SearchParamsView.description:
One request's stage parameters. Round-trips: this is both what the trace
reports and what the playground posts back as `params`.

budget_tokens.description: `None` returns all `limit` chunks — the budget is the caller's choice.

folder_id.description:
`null` for a thread in no folder, and for one in a folder the
caller cannot see.

hits.description: The best matches, up to three.

match_count.description: How many places in the thread match.

SearchTraceView.description: Per-stage trace: what each stage saw, in the order it saw it.

budget_dropped.description: Chunks the token budget dropped, in the order they would have come.

fts_query.description:
The FTS5 MATCH expression actually issued — user text is never passed
through raw.

knn_kernel.description: Which widening kernel the KNN scan used.

knn_skipped.description:
Why the vector stage did not run, so BM25 alone answered. Absent when
it ran.

rerank_skipped.description: Why the rerank stage did not run, when `params.rerank` asked for it.

floor.description:
A score at or above this and below the threshold commits at
`semantic_floor_window_ms`; equal to the threshold turns the middle
band off.

max_wait_ms.description: The longest a pause waits, whatever the score.

silence_duration_ms.description:
Where a pause that could not be scored commits, and the window the
`server_vad` engine runs this eagerness on.

threshold.description: A Smart Turn score at or above this commits the turn, `0.0..=1.0`.

SeriesMeta.description: Identity of one series, with the colour slot it wears everywhere.

folded.description:
On the folded "Other" series only: how many entities it sums, so a
legend can say "Other (49 aliases)" instead of hiding the tail's size.
`null` on every named series.

label.description:
What to print — a key id resolves to its name here, an upstream id to
its name, an alias is itself.

local.description:
True for a locally-served model — it can never appear in a spend chart,
because its money cost is a real zero.

slot.description:
Chart colour slot 0..5, or `null` for the neutral "Other" bucket.

Assigned from the entity's position in the gateway's own sorted list of
aliases, **not** from its rank in this response: a filter that drops a
series must not repaint the survivors, or a reader who learned "qwen is
teal" is being lied to.

ServedModel.description:
An alias a stage asked for, the one that answered when it was another,
and (for the text-to-speech stage) the voice.

ServerFacts.description:
What the live server says about itself: the numbers every point is
derived from, and the build facts `/props` carries on engines that report
them.

chat_template_caps.description:
`/props` `chat_template_caps`, the boolean entries. Empty when the
engine sends none (ik).

kv_unified.description:
Whether every slot draws its KV cells from one shared pool: then *S* is the whole pool, and
requests running
together must fit in it side by side — a full pool aborts every
running request. From the server where it says (ik's top-level
`n_ctx` against the per-slot one), else from the row's effective
settings (`kv_unified`, or `parallel` left on auto); `None` when
neither says, read as split.

speculative.description: Whether any slot reports speculative decoding (official `/slots`).

total_ctx.description:
The whole context, where the engine reports it (ik's top-level
`/props` `n_ctx`).

Sourced_Nullable_string.description: A value and the level it came from; `source: null` when no level sets it.

Sourced_TurnDetectionMode.description: A value and the level it came from; `source: null` when no level sets it.

Sourced_boolean.description: A value and the level it came from; `source: null` when no level sets it.

SpeechCaps.description:
The `speech` object of a text-to-speech model's capabilities. Absent
fields are unknown, as everywhere in the schema.

inline_tags.description:
What inline tags in `input` do: `none` (stripped, never read out),
`fixed` (the ones in `tags` are rendered, stage directions mapped
onto them, the rest stripped), `free` (every `[tag]` is rendered).

instructions.description:
What `instructions` do: `none` (dropped — said in `x-lmgw-speech`),
`style` (a speaking style for the voice), `voice_design` (the voice
is designed from them), `passthrough` (sent; the model reads them —
it declares an instruction option, or lmgw knows its engine reads
one anyway — and decides what they do).

instructions_required.description:
A request without instructions is refused (`instructions_required`)
unless the row has a default description.

languages.description:
ISO 639-1 codes the model speaks; `language` takes them (lmgw sends
each in the model's own spelling).

sample_rate.description:
The sample rate of its audio, in Hz, as its last answer through lmgw
said (a streamed answer's PCM has no header of its own; the same
figure is the `x-lmgw-sample-rate` header on it). Absent until the
model has answered once since lmgw started.

streaming.description:
`stream_format` (`sse` or `audio`, `response_format: pcm`) works on
this row: it runs in streaming mode.

tags.description: The tags a `fixed` model renders, written `[tag]`.

SpeechForm.description:
The TTS panel's widgets, raw. Parsed by `speech_body` so the "Request"
disclosure and the actual call are literally the same bytes.

instructions.description:
OpenAI's `instructions`: delivery and style guidance, forwarded as the
engine's `instruction` option.

language.description:
Language code passed to models whose contract accepts one; the
transcription panel sends the same field.

options.description: Engine options as JSON text, sent as the body's `options`.

speed.description:
`speed`: a positive multiplier, on models that support speed control
(audio.cpp rejects it on models that do not, rather than ignoring it).

stream.description: Stream the answer as server-sent events of PCM.

SpeechFormInput.description:
The TTS panel's widgets, raw. Parsed by `speech_body` so the "Request"
disclosure and the actual call are literally the same bytes.

instructions.description:
OpenAI's `instructions`: delivery and style guidance, forwarded as the
engine's `instruction` option.

language.description:
Language code passed to models whose contract accepts one; the
transcription panel sends the same field.

options.description: Engine options as JSON text, sent as the body's `options`.

speed.description:
`speed`: a positive multiplier, on models that support speed control
(audio.cpp rejects it on models that do not, rather than ignoring it).

stream.description: Stream the answer as server-sent events of PCM.

source.description:
The level the text came from; `row` when the text-to-speech model's
own description stands in for it.

cpu.description:
An audio model that runs on the CPU: the GPU hold does not stop it, a
benchmark run's lease does.

fallback.description:
What answers instead while the model is blocked; `null` off this
machine, or when the model has no usable fallback.

fallback_unusable.description: A fallback the model names that cannot stand in, and why.

inherited.description:
What the levels below the thread give: the alias the thread uses once
its own override is cleared; equal to `alias` when the thread sets
none.

local.description:
`false` for an alias served off this machine; `null` when the alias
does not resolve.

managed.description:
A model lmgw starts itself: the GPU hold and a benchmark run's lease
apply to it.

source.description: The level `alias` came from; `null` with no alias.

StageHitView.description:
One candidate as a stage saw it. `score` is BM25 (negative, lower is
better), cosine, or the reranker's — read next to the stage it came from.

score.description:
`null` when the embedder or reranker returned NaN, which `serde_json`
writes as `null`.

skipped.description:
Rerank stage only: the reranker did not score this candidate (its pair
was over the model's input limit); `score` is then its fused score and
it ranks behind the scored ones. Absent otherwise.

Stat.description:
Median, min and max of one metric over a point's repetitions, and the raw
values in repetition order.

oneOf.description: Plain text, sent as a JSON string.

JSON text (an object, an array, `null` for the types that take no
state), checked to parse and sent as typed.

StaticCaps.description:
The statically derived capabilities a `/props` read is compared with. Each
has the shape the `/v1/models` capabilities object gives it.

StrList.description:
A list of short names as a patch carries it (`modes`): a JSON array, or a
comma/whitespace-separated string for the same reason `KeyMap` takes
text.

SuiteParams.description:
What a run was asked to do. The suite constants are stored
beside the caller's choices, so a stored run says exactly what it measured
without anyone having to know which suite version meant what.

phases.description: The selected phases, in suite order; `load` is always among them.

repetitions.description: Repetitions of every point (and of the mixed phase).

oneOf.description: Pick one of the named options.
Rate on 2 to 10 ordered levels.
Yes or no.

SystemOneResponse.description:
`POST /v1/systemone`'s answer, as the upstream sent it.

`model` is the upstream's own: the versioned id that answered on TypeSafe
(`jev-1.13.0`), a dated id on OpenRouter, the server's `--alias` on
llama.cpp. lmgw does not write the requested name back; which alias
answered is `x-lmgw-fallback`'s to say (§2.1).

answers.description: One answer per question, under the question's key.

provider.description: OpenRouter's extension: the provider that answered.

SystemOneUsage.description:
What a request processed: lmgw logs `input_tokens` as the row's prompt
tokens and `output_tokens` as its completion tokens, and prices them from
its own price rows (§2.6).

cost.description:
OpenRouter's extension: what the request cost there, in USD. Relayed,
never read: lmgw prices from its own rows.

output_tokens.description:
Always 0 on llama.cpp; TypeSafe and OpenRouter report a non-zero
count, which Jev's price does not charge.

Takeover.description: `?takeover=`: whether a bind may take its thread from another session.

oneOf.description: Take the thread over (what a bind without the parameter does).
Never: refuse while another session is bound to the thread.

Ask first (WebRTC calls only, realtime calls design §2.8): a thread
held when the call's channel opens makes the call wait,
`lmgw.session.bind_pending`, for the client's
`lmgw.session.take_over` or the holder's end.

flags.description: Each checkbox, by the request field it sets.

json.description: Raw JSON merged into the request last.

values.description: Each field's text, by the request field it fills.

request.description: Relayed to audio.cpp's generic task endpoint untouched; its shape is the task's own and is not modeled here.

TemplateSignals.description:
What the chat template's own text says about reasoning, effort selection
and tool-call rendering. Pure text heuristics: a template that does it
through indirection reads as absent.

effort_default.description: The effort it falls back to, verbatim.

effort_levels.description: The effort levels it compares against, in canonical order.

enable_thinking_default.description: The default of `enable_thinking`, when the template states one.

parallel_tool_calls.description: The template loops over `tool_calls`: several calls per turn.

reasoning_effort_var.description: The template reads a reasoning-effort variable of any name.

thinking_marker.description: The first marker that matched, verbatim.

thinking_markers.description: The template renders a reasoning trace somewhere.

tool_call_format.description: The native tool-call syntax family it renders.

TestUsage.description: A test call's token usage, as the model reported it.

TextCompletion.description: Relayed as the upstream sends it.

TextCompletionChunk.description: One frame, relayed as the upstream sends it: `data: <this object>`, repeated, ending with the literal `data: [DONE]`.

Thread.description:
One Chat thread with what an open thread shows: its list row, what its
voice resolves to now, and (where it is read whole) whether its last
reply can be continued.

agent_id.description: The agent the thread was opened from, if any.

archived_at.description: When the thread was archived; `null` while it is active.

continue.description:
Whether the last reply can be continued. Present where the thread
is read whole, as `POST /chat/api/folders/{id}/current` answers it.

folder_id.description: The folder the thread is in; `null` for none.

kb_budget_tokens.description:
The retrieval budget of `auto` mode in tokens; `null` for the Chat's
setting.

kb_ids.description: Knowledge bases the thread searches, by id.

kind.description:
`chat`, or `admin` for a thread that drives the gateway's own
configuration (never listed for a device key).

last_message_at.description:
When its newest message was written, in unix seconds; `null` for a
thread without messages. An ongoing folder's idle rollover is
measured from it: a client that shows when the conversation moves
on reads it here rather than timing the turns it saw.

mcp_tools.description:
The tool servers the thread's turns use; empty for a plain chat. A
thread with `lmgw` (the self-admin toolset) among them is listed for a
device key only when the device may use lmgw's admin tools.

model_alias.description: The alias the thread's turns go to.

pinned.description:
Pinned threads are listed first and are never archived or deleted
by the sweep.

profile_id.description:
The personality profile the thread talks with
(`GET /chat/api/profiles`); `null` for none ("Default").

purge_at.description:
When an archived thread will be deleted; `null` while it is active,
pinned, or when deleting is switched off.

reasoning_enabled.description:
Reasoning overrides sent with every turn; `null` leaves the route's
default.

stop.description: Stop sequences; empty leaves the route's default.

temperature.description:
Sampling overrides sent with every turn; `null` leaves the route's
default.

temporary.description:
The thread lives in memory only and is gone at the gateway's next
start unless it is kept.

updated_at.description: Moves with every change to the thread and every new message.

voice_resolved.description:
