ThreadTask.description:
One of a thread's tasks: still running, or ended with its result on its
way into the thread.

id.description: lmgw's id of the task: the cancel route's `{task}`.

status.description:
`working` or `input_required` while it runs; `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled` or `abandoned` once it ended.

status_message.description: The server's last word on it, when it gave one.

task_id.description: The server's id of the task.

ttl_ms.description:
How long the server keeps it, as it stated; `null` when it stated
none.

waiting_for.description:
What it waits for, when it waits: a device that is not connected
(its tasks are asked about again when it links), a turn of the
thread that runs (a result enters the thread once it ended), or the
decision on the calls the thread's last reply waits on.

ThreadVoice.description:
A thread's own voice settings. Every field is optional and absent when
unset: an absent field takes the Chat's voice settings.

asr_alias.description:
The speech-to-text alias for dictation, voice mode and audio
attachments.

language.description:
The language the user speaks, a two-letter ISO 639-1 code, or `auto`
to let the speech-to-text model detect it.

read_aloud.description: Read every reply aloud as it streams.

reply_language.description:
The language replies are in, a two-letter code, or `auto` to follow
the language the user speaks.

seed.description:
The thread's text-to-speech seed, so one thread keeps one voice on a
model that draws its voice. Set on first use.

speech_style.description:
The speaking style the text-to-speech model is given; an empty text
is none for this thread.

tts_alias.description: The text-to-speech alias for read-aloud and voice mode.

voice.description: A voice of that text-to-speech model.

ThreadsFate.description: What a folder delete does with the threads in the folder.

oneOf.description: The threads stay, in no folder.
The threads are deleted with the folder.

Threshold.description:
A question's threshold: an answer whose confidence (`choice`, `score`)
or certainty, max(p, 1 − p) (`noul`), is below it needs attention.

measured.description: Where the value was measured; `null`: not measured.

value.description:
From 0 to 1. 0 is "never needs attention", what an unmeasured
question has.

ThresholdInput.description:
A question's threshold: an answer whose confidence (`choice`, `score`)
or certainty, max(p, 1 − p) (`noul`), is below it needs attention.

measured.description: Where the value was measured; `null`: not measured.

value.description:
From 0 to 1. 0 is "never needs attention", what an unmeasured
question has.

Timeline.description: The sampled timeline stored with a run.

TimelineSample.description:
One stored sample (spaced `interval_ms` apart); sums over the devices,
temperature is the hottest one's.

clock_events.description:
The OR of the NVML clock-event reason bits seen since the previous stored
sample.

Timings.description:
Server-measured prefill and decode timings of a local model: the `stats`
frame (live per token while it streams) and the `done` frame's final
`timings`.

cache_n.description: Prompt tokens served from the KV cache.

draft_n.description: Draft tokens proposed (speculative or MTP decoding).

predicted_ms.description: Milliseconds spent generating; absent when llama.cpp gave no finite number.

predicted_per_second.description: Tokens generated per second; absent when llama.cpp gave no finite number.

prompt_ms.description: Milliseconds spent on the prompt; absent when llama.cpp gave no finite number.

prompt_n.description: Prompt tokens actually processed this turn (the cache excluded).

prompt_per_second.description: Prompt tokens processed per second; absent when llama.cpp gave no finite number.

TokenizeRequest.description: Every key but model is forwarded to the backend's own /tokenize verbatim. Refused with 501 not_supported_error on any backend but a real llama-server — an id from a tokenizer the backend does not run would be a hidden approximation.

content.description: A string, or a mixed array of strings and token ids.

model.description: Required: llama-server's router mode has no other way to pick a backend. A missing model is a 400 naming GET /v1/models.

tokens.description: An array of integer token ids, or — with_pieces — an array of {id, piece} (piece a string, or a byte array when it is not valid UTF-8).

ToolArgsFrame.description: A fragment of a call's JSON arguments, in order.

format.description:
The native syntax family the template renders (`qwen-xml`,
`hermes-json`, …), `provider` for cloud, `unknown` when the template
renders tools with none of the known markers. Informational.

kind.description:
`native` (lmgw returns structured `tool_calls`), `none` (the template
renders no tools; aux/audio rows), `text` (the template renders tools
in a syntax llama-server has no parser for, so calls may arrive as
prose the caller must read itself).

parallel.description:
The template can render more than one call per turn. Absent for cloud
models, which publish nothing about it.

ToolEntryView.description: One tool the gateway can serve, with its provenance and current state.

available.description: Offered right now: `enabled` **and** its source's condition holds.

moved_from.description:
The name it would have if no other source offered a tool of that
name: set when a collision gave it its server's name as a prefix.

moved_reason.description:
Why it moved: who else claims `moved_from`, and whether that
claim is only a server's last listing (it is not connected now).

name.description: Fully-qualified exposed name — the key the switch is stored under.

stale.description: A disable record whose tool the gateway no longer offers.

ToolReadyFrame.description:
A Chat `tool` frame whose `event` is `ready` (also the `data` of a bound
realtime session's `lmgw.chat.frame` for it): a call's arguments are
complete, before it runs — what a host that shows the call's view at once
needs (client-apps design §7.5).

call_id.description: The call's id, as its `result` frame carries it.

index.description: The call's position in its turn.

name.description: The tool's exposed name, as the model called it.

needs_approval.description:
The call waits for an approval and does not run now: an `approval`
frame follows. `false` for a call that runs (a resumed turn's decided
calls included). Absent from an lmgw before 2026-10-09.

server_label.description: The label the tool came from; `null` for a client's own function.

ui_resource.description: The UI resource the tool links to, as on the result frame.

ToolResultFrame.description:
A Chat `tool` frame whose `event` is `result` (also the `data` of a
bound realtime session's `lmgw.chat.frame` for it), as an MCP Apps host
reads it. MCP's `CallToolResult` for the view is `{content,
structuredContent: structured_content, isError: is_error}`.

call_id.description: The call's id, as its `ready` frame carries it.

content.description:
The MCP result's `content` blocks as the server sent them (resource
URIs namespaced as `/mcp` sends them; images in full — no bound of
lmgw's own, a device's result is bounded by `mcp.host_max_message_mb`
on its link); a tool lmgw runs itself, or a call that never reached
a server, says its result in the same shape. Absent from an lmgw
before 2026-10-09: `output` as one text block then.

index.description: The call's position in its turn.

name.description: The tool's exposed name (`<prefix>__<tool>`).

server_label.description:
The label the tool came from: a server's tool prefix (else its
name), or a built-in toolset's (`lmgw`, `docs`, `kb`).

structured_content.description:
The MCP result's `structuredContent`, for the view. The model was
given it only when `content` is empty.

task.description: For a call that started an MCP task: which. Absent otherwise.

ui_resource.description:
The UI resource the tool links to (`_meta.ui.resourceUri`),
namespaced as `/mcp` serves it: `resources/read` it there.

ToolSourceView.description:
One source of tools, so a source that currently offers none (a disabled
server, self-admin off, a server that has not connected) is still visible
with the reason: the per-tool rows cannot carry that.

disabled_count.description: How many of those the owner has switched off.

kind.description: `builtin | server`.

label.description:
The label a thread or a `{"type":"mcp"}` block attaches: `lmgw`, `docs`,
or a server's prefix/name.

tool_count.description: Tools this source contributes to the inventory right now.

ToolStartFrame.description: A tool call starting to stream: its position and name.

id.description: The model's id of the call; only a turn without tools says it.

index.description: The call's position in its turn.

name.description: The tool's exposed name.

TranscribedClip.description: One clip `voice_transcribe` wrote a transcript for.

answered_by.description: The fallback alias that answered in place of the one asked, else `null`.

by.description: Who wrote it, in a sentence.

transcript_source.description:
`asr:<model>`: the model the transcript came from. When a fallback
answered, that model's name.

anyOf.description: A turn model decides when the speaker is done.
A turn is what is spoken while the talk key is held.

TurnDetectionMode.description: How voice mode detects the end of the user's turn.

UnpricedModel.description:
One model that resolves to no price at all — an entry on the "why is my
spend incomplete" worklist.

`requests` is what it has already cost that nobody can name, from the
rollup. A configured alias that has never been called is still listed, at
`0`: it is about to be the same problem.

UpdateStatus.description:
A build's update badge state: the result of the periodic (or
"Check now") comparison of the resolved ref and extras against the last
verified run.

`Some` on a build view once the build has been checked against a run it
can be compared with; `None` before its first check, and for a build with
no succeeded (or unverified) run. A status with no `reasons` is **up to
date as of `checked_at`** — `has_update` is what the Backends nav
badge counts. What could not be checked is in `errors`, never in `reasons`:
a rate-limited forge is not an update.

The server re-evaluates the stored remote facts against the build and its
runs on every read, so a run that builds the new head clears "master moved"
at once, and an edit shows "definition changed since last run" at once —
neither waits for the next check.

checked_at.description: When the remote facts behind this status were fetched (RFC 3339).

errors.description:
What the check could not find out, one sentence each, starting
`check failed:` — a forge's rate limit (with its reset time), a remote
that did not answer, a ref that no longer exists. Shown, never counted
as an update.

reasons.description:
Human sentences, one per reason (`"master +37 commits"`,
`"master moved (abc1234 → def5678)"` when the count is not known
without fetching, `"PR #1234 pushed"`, `"PR #1234 closed unmerged"`,
`"definition changed since last run (ref, extras)"`). A PR the forge
reports merged reads `"PR #1234 merged upstream and contained in your
base — drop it"` only once the base is proven (locally, no fetch) to
already hold its merge or head commit; otherwise `"PR #1234 merged
upstream at <date>; your base doesn't contain it yet — it's still
merged into your build"` — the same non-committal wording whether that
was proven false or is simply unknown.

ref_moved.description:
The base `ref` itself moved (a branch or tag; a pinned commit never
updates).

file.description: The stored file; absent for a refused one.

name.description: The name the part carried.

reason.description: Why it was not added, or what it replaced.

UploadVerdict.description: What became of one uploaded file.

oneOf.description: Stored and queued for ingest.
A file of that name existed; its content was replaced and queued again.
The same name with the same bytes: nothing to do.
The same bytes already in the base under another name.

Not stored; `reason` says why (images and audio are refused, as is an
empty or unreadable file).

aliases.description: Enabled explicit aliases pointing at this upstream.

UpstreamLlamaFacts.description:
What an external llama.cpp server said about itself, or a router about
one model (`GET /props`). Asked in the
background, one probe per row at a time, and kept until the row is
edited, unreachable, refuses a medium or is tested.

base_url.description: The base URL it was asked at.

cached.description:
The answer stands until an event drops it. `false` for a probe that
found nothing worth keeping (a router that has not loaded the model,
a server that did not answer): it is asked again on the next use.

model.description:
Empty for the server itself: a llama-server that is no router serves
one model whatever a request names, so its facts hold for every model
of the row. Under a router, the upstream model this entry is about,
as the row's aliases (or an `expose_all` request) name it.

probing.description: Being asked now, or waiting for the row's probe.

props.description:
The facts, when the server stated them: its build, one slot's
context and its modalities. `None` is unknown; `unknown` says why.

read_at.description: Unix seconds of the answer shown; `None` while the first is on its way.

router.description:
The server is a llama-server router (only on the entry with an empty
`model`): it states its build and nothing about a model, so `props`
carries the build alone, and the facts are on the per-model entries.
Defaulted, so a gateway older than the field still parses.

unknown.description:
Why the facts are unknown: the server's own answer (an old build's
404, a 401), or why the last probe found nothing.

UpstreamModelEntry.description:
One entry of an upstream's live catalog (`catalog::ModelInfo`), including
the entries hidden from `/v1/models` — which is why the dashboard reads
this rather than `/v1/models`. Every field the catalog does not publish is
`None`: unknown, never a default.

id.description: Bare, as the upstream names it (no expose prefix).

price_prompt.description: USD per token, the upstream's verbatim decimal string.

reasoning_enabled.description:
Whether it thinks by default, where the catalog says — what tells a
`fixed` model that always reasons from one that never does.

UpstreamPriceSync.description: What a price sync did to one upstream.

error.description:
The catalog fetch failed; nothing was synced for this upstream. Not
fatal to the run as a whole — one unreachable provider should not stop
every other upstream's prices from refreshing. `null` when it was
asked.

not_synced.description:
Per field of the catalog's pricing object, how many models had their
token prices synced here and publish that field with a value other
than zero that went into no row. Left out on purpose: `image` (a
price per *input* image, not a generated one),
`web_search` (no route carries a hosted search), and the fields lmgw
does not model, such as `internal_reasoning`, `image_output`,
`overrides` or `discount`. Also a `request` fee or cache rate that is
not a price (`"-1"`, unparseable). A model counted in
`unpriced_models` had nothing synced and is not counted here again.
Empty when nothing published was left out.

rows_removed.description:
Catalog `per_request` rows deleted because their model, priced here,
no longer publishes a `request` fee at all.

rows_written.description:
Rows created or updated: one `per_mtok` row per priced model and
scope, and a `per_request` row beside it where the catalog states a
fee.

catalog_all_modalities.description:
The catalog request asks for every output modality
(`GET …/models?output_modalities=all`), so OpenRouter lists its
decision, embedding, rerank, speech, transcription, image and video
models too. Only an `openai` row of kind `generic` sends it; on by
default, off for an endpoint that refuses it (Gemini's
OpenAI-compatible one).

extra_headers.description: Names only; values are redacted server-side.

kind.description:
`generic | llama_server | audio_cpp`. `llama_server` goes with
protocol `llama_cpp` or `anthropic`.

llama_facts.description:
A `llama_cpp` row's server: what `GET /props` said, when, or why it
is unknown — one entry for the server, and for a router one more per
model (its `model`). Empty on every other protocol,
and on a `llama_cpp` row until a chat request or its Test makes lmgw
ask in the background.

protocol.description:
`openai | anthropic | gemini | llama_cpp`. `llama_cpp` is llama.cpp's
own server (llama-server, ik_llama.cpp) and is always kind
`llama_server`.

UsageCell.description:
One (bucket, series) cell.

Money is integer **micro-units** of the configured currency everywhere on
this plane; a float that has been through JSON twice does not add up.

audio_in_ms.description:
What the requests processed besides tokens, as **measured** or
reported by the provider: input audio in milliseconds, input
characters, generated images. A request that measured nothing adds 0,
so these are measured totals, and before the series' `units_since`
nothing was recorded at all.

cost_unknown_audio_in_ms.description:
The same quantities of the requests `cost_unknown_requests` counts,
so the remainder can say what it holds beside its tokens.

cost_unknown_requests.description:
What `cost_micro` does **not** cover. Every total that is displayed is
obliged to show this beside it — a cost figure with a
silent hole in it is worse than no cost figure.

decode_tokens.description:
Local-model throughput as a ratio pair: tok/s is Σtokens / Σms, never a
mean of per-request rates.

series.description: The series key this cell belongs to (`""` when ungrouped).

tokens_cache_write.description:
Input written *into* the prompt cache — Anthropic's 1.25x tier, the
dearest input a window can contain. Zero everywhere else, because no
other provider bills a cache write.

tokens_cached.description:
Input served from the provider's prompt cache, billed at the cheap
read rate.

tokens_in.description:
**Total** input, cache included — the same meaning `ir::Usage`'s
`prompt_tokens` carries, so fresh (uncached) input is
`tokens_in - tokens_cached - tokens_cache_write` and never a fourth
stored number that could drift from the other three.

UsedBy.description:
What uses a profile, computed when it is read: what a delete would
clear.

threads.description: Stored threads that picked it, archived ones included.

Variant.description:
What a cell sends: the form as written, or one of the two perturbations
(labs-store design §2.6).

oneOf.description: Every `choice` description `null`, and no `noul` criteria.
Each `choice` question's options in reverse.

Verdict.description: How one metric moved (by the regression rule).

oneOf.description: Within the band: max(threshold, noise).
One of the two runs did not measure it.

Both runs measured it, but at different points — another prompt
length, depth or stream count, as when one run stopped early. The delta is kept as
information; it is no verdict, so
it counts neither as a regression nor as an improvement.

error.description: Why.

VoiceModels.description: The models one spoken turn went through.

VoiceName.description: The voice the text-to-speech model is asked for.

inherits.description:
Settings → Realtime's default voice, when no name is named: applied by
voice mode, never sent as the voice.

name.description:
The voice to ask for; `null`: none is named, and voice mode's own
chain decides.

note.description: Why a voice set at a less specific level is not used here.

source.description:
Where `name` came from. With no name, `realtime` when Settings →
Realtime's default voice is where that chain starts, else `null`.

VoiceProblem.description: Something that blocks a voice feature.

code.description:
`not_configured`, `unresolved`, or `voice_needs_transcript` (a voice
clip the text-to-speech model cannot clone without its transcript).

asr.description: The speech-to-text stage: dictation, voice mode, audio attachments.

audio_input.description: Whether a voice turn goes to the chat model as audio, and why not.

language.description:
The language the user speaks, ISO 639-1; `value: null` is none, the
speech-to-text model detects it.

language_notes.description: Where a stage's model does not take its language as set.

problems.description:
What blocks a voice feature now: a stage with no alias, or one whose
alias no longer resolves.

read_aloud.description: Whether replies are read aloud as they stream.

realtime.description: Whether voice mode may bind the thread.

reply_language.description:
The language replies are in, ISO 639-1: the thread's, Settings', else
the spoken one (`source: speech_in`); `value: null` is none, the reply
follows the user.

seed.description:
The thread's text-to-speech seed; `null` until its first use draws
one.

speech_style.description: The speech instructions the read-aloud uses.

tts.description: The text-to-speech stage: read-aloud and voice mode.

turn_detection.description: How voice mode detects the end of a turn.

voice.description: The voice the text-to-speech model is asked for.

anyOf.description:
The text-to-speech model's own description of its voice (a speech
style only).

The reply language only: none is set for it, so it is the language the
user speaks.

VoiceSource.description: The level a value came from.

VoiceTiming.description:
A spoken reply's timing: each stage measured from the one before,
`to_first_audio_ms` their sum from the end of speech, `cold` the stages
that loaded during the turn.

cold.description: The stages that loaded during the turn.

first_clause.description:
`announcement` when the first clause said was an announcement of a
skipped block.

input.description: How the turn reached the chat model; absent with audio input off.

input_why.description: Why the transcript went where audio input is on.

reasoning_ms.description:
How long the chat model reasoned before its first token (part of
`first_token_ms`); absent when it did not reason.

transcript_wait_ms.description:
How long the first output was held for the turn's transcript; absent
on the transcript path.

VramEstimate.description:
The GPU cost of the weights and the KV cache at the trained context; a
chat model's is laid out as its row is charged, for one slot. Compute
buffers depend on a row's settings and are in the plan's footprint, not
here.

kv_cache_bytes_at_full_ctx_f16.description:
KV cache for `context_length` tokens at f16; null when the header
lacks what the estimate needs.

VramKvPool.description: One guarded model's shared KV pool.

capacity_tokens.description:
The pool's size in tokens, as the running container was started
with it.

queue.description: Requests waiting for room, head first.

releasing.description:
Requests that ended without a normal completion and keep their
reservation until llama-server lets go of their slots.

reserved_tokens.description: Σ (prompt + max output) of the requests in flight and releasing.

VramKvPoolWaiter.description: One request waiting for room in a pool.

peak_extra_bytes.description:
What one generation of a resident image pipeline has been measured to
need *above* its idle residency, and what admission keeps free for it. `None` for every
other class, and for an image
model that has not generated anything yet — `note` says which.

pending_bytes.description:
What a `ready` audio container will still load on its first request,
kept free by admission on top of the measured use: its expected residency less what it was
read holding at rest,
or all of it where that could not be read. `None` once loaded, and for
every other class.

state.description:
`starting | ready` as the runtime registry holds it, or `reserved` for
a start the scheduler has admitted whose container is not up yet.

budget_mb.description:
`0` = the device's real total, as the driver reports it (NVML on
NVIDIA, amdgpu sysfs on AMD).

fallback_on_external.description:
Fall back when VRAM outside lmgw's control is short. Absent reads as on, like the server's
own default.

VramSettingsPatch.description:
VRAM admission control. Every field is optional so one knob moves
without restating the rest.

fallback_on_external.description: Fall back when VRAM outside lmgw's control is short.

VramStatus.description:
`GET /api/vram` and the `vram` SSE frame — measured figures and
estimated ones are separate fields on
purpose: the UI must be able to say which is which.

active.description:
Whether admission is actually arbitrating; false is explained by
`inactive_reason`.

benchmark.description: The benchmark run holding the card, if one does: no local model is admitted until it ends.

draining.description:
Resident model ids that are busy or still starting while hold is
active — visible continuously, not only in the one-shot `hold_set`
response. Empty whenever hold is not active.

external_trigger_active.description: Whether the outside-VRAM fallback can fire right now.

external_trigger_reason.description:
Why it cannot, when it cannot (the switch, admission, the hold, no
telemetry, an unattributable lmgw model).

free_measured.description:
False when `free_bytes` was derived from the estimate rather than read
from the driver.

hold_active.description:
The `hold.active` setting — hold is a switch on
the resolve/start paths, orthogonal to `enabled`/`active` above.

hold_fallback_alias.description:
`settings.hold.fallback_alias`, for the titlebar pill and the
settings page to show what a held chat request falls back to.

kv_pools.description:
The token ledger of every guarded unified-KV chat model with a request
in flight or waiting — `vram::VramView`'s
`kv_pools`. Absent from an older gateway's frame, hence the default.

lmgw_share_bytes.description:
lmgw's own share of the pooled devices' used memory, measured per
process. `None` when it
cannot be measured — see `external_trigger_reason`.

outside_share_bytes.description:
Used memory that is not lmgw's — games, the desktop, other apps.
`None` exactly when `lmgw_share_bytes` is.

telemetry.description: Where the measured numbers come from, verbatim.

oneOf.description: Answered: waiting for ICE and DTLS.
ICE and DTLS-SRTP are up; `oai-events` has not opened.
`oai-events` is open; the bind runs.

`takeover=ask` found its thread held: it waits for the client's
`lmgw.session.take_over` or the holder's end (`held_by`).
Its session runs.

It let go: its slot is back, and it only delivers its last events
before it closes, at most `realtime.ping_interval_s`.

allowance_ms.description:
The playout allowance in ms (calls design §5.3): NetEQ's part of the
delay, which the window's end, drained and a barge-in's heard take.
`null` before the call's audio out runs.

candidate.description:
Its one host candidate: the local address its POST arrived on, on
its group's UDP port.

client_jitter_ms.description:
The client's interarrival jitter on lmgw's stream, by its latest
receiver report, in ms (to 0.1); `null` while `closing`.

connected_at.description: When ICE and DTLS connected (RFC 3339 UTC); `null` before.

egress_loss.description:
The share of lmgw's packets the client lost, 0 to 1, by its latest
receiver report (to 0.001); `null` while `closing`.

group.description: The socket group it lives on: the listener its POST came in on.

held_by.description:
Who holds its thread while it is `pending`, as `voice.bound.by`
names a client.

ingress_loss.description:
The share of the client's packets lmgw lost over the last second, 0
to 1 (to 0.001); `null` for a second in which none arrived, and while
`closing`.

jitter_buffer_ms.description:
The latest playout report's `jitter_buffer_ms` (to 0.1): NetEQ's own
delay as the client's `getStats` gives it, the allowance seen from
the phone.

key.description:
The key that made it (`device:phone`, `owner:…`); `null` for an
anonymous caller.

playout_report_age_ms.description:
How long ago the latest playout report arrived, whatever it carried,
in ms: the age of `jitter_buffer_ms`. `null` before the first.

receiver_report_age_ms.description:
How long ago the client's latest receiver report arrived, in ms: the
age of `egress_loss`, `client_jitter_ms` and the round trip it fed.
A client sends one every few seconds; `null` before the first, and
while `closing`.

remote.description: Where the client's last authenticated traffic came from.

round_trip_ms.description:
The session's round trip, in ms: the least of the last five the
client's receiver reports measured, as the playout allowance and the
barge-in margin take it. `null` before the first report reached the
call's audio out, and while `closing`.

session.description: Its realtime session's id, once the session runs.

thread.description: The Chat thread its session is bound to.

WebRtcGroup.description: Which listener a socket group serves.

oneOf.description: The plain listener's: stock clients.
The device listener's: paired devices.

`realtime.webrtc_enabled` was off at the gateway's start: a call on
its listener is refused 503 naming the setting.
Not bound: its listener does not serve, or it is moving with it.
Bound on `addrs`.

Its bind failed, or its sockets were lost; `error` says why. Its
listener serves on, and a call there is refused 503 naming it.

WebRtcGroupStatus.description: One socket group: the sockets of the listener a call's POST came in on.

addrs.description:
Its sockets, as `udp://` addresses: one per address of its listener.
Empty unless `bound`.

error.description:
Why it is not bound, with state `failed`: the bind error naming the
address, or the call driver's stop.

rule.description:
The rule that binds it, naming its settings: the plain listener's
`bind_addr` and `realtime.webrtc_port`, or the device listener's
addresses and port.

calls.description:
The live calls, oldest first, those still delivering their last
events (`closing`) included.

dropped.description:
Datagrams no call accepted, dropped unanswered since lmgw started
(the count outlives the call driver, which a panic starts again).

enabled.description:
`realtime.webrtc_enabled` as the gateway's last start read it: the
setting applies at the next start, so a saved value may differ until
then.

groups.description: The socket groups: the plain listener's, then the device listener's.

apiKeyHeader.description: The same keys, in the header Anthropic SDKs send them in.
apiKeyHeader.name: x-api-key

bearer.description: An lmgw API key: a client, owner or agent key. A paired device presents none: it authenticates by its client certificate on the device listener, which refuses a bearer there 400 credential_on_device_listener. A bearer key a device was paired with before TLS (lmgw-device-…) is refused 401 device_key_unknown on every listener: pair the device again.

session.description: The dashboard's own session cookie. Same-origin only, and only ever an owner row.
session.name: lmgw_session

info.description: lmgw's own HTTP API: the inference plane (OpenAI-, Anthropic- and llama.cpp-compatible, plus MCP), the device (Chat) API paired clients use, the agent run API agents use, and the dashboard that configures the gateway.
info.title: lmgw

get.description: Every agent in the catalog, with its warnings, requirements and last-run summary.

post.description: Imports an agent from an exported manifest file (paste uses this same route). replace overwrites an id that already exists; validate_only runs the checks and reports without writing.

schema.description:
`POST /api/agents/import` and `lmgw__agent_set` — the same report either
way. Errors are not in here: they are the 400 body (`ApiError`), because a
manifest that does not validate was not imported at all.

config_unbound.description:
Mount slots this agent has and nothing has bound: an
export never carries a host path, so an imported agent arrives with its
`directory` and `file` fields empty and the importer says which folder.

dropped_config.description:
Stored config keys the **new** manifest no longer declares, removed with
the manifest that declared them (the same rule applies to every replace). Keeping them
would leave a row that fails validation
on every run and cannot be fixed from its own config form.

replaced.description: An existing agent was overwritten (`replace=1`), keeping its config.

warnings.description: A missing server label or tool: the agent is saved, Start is disabled.

schema.title: AgentImportReport

post.x-lmgw-confirm-note: replace overwrites an agent id that already exists here

get.description: One run with its rows: the executor's live buffer while it is in flight, the stored result once it has ended. Ownership is checked before existence, so a run that belongs to another caller and a missing one get the same refusal.

schema.description: `GET /api/agents/runs/{job_id}` — the job plus its rows.

batch.description:
The agent's current review shape, so the table can be drawn from a run
alone — including one finished last week, which is what "reopen this
run's review" needs. For a ledger run its `columns` carry the undeclared
keys the events brought, appended after the declared ones in first-seen
order.

log.description:
The run log: `log` events, rejected events, and the lines lmgw itself
wrote. Empty for an in-process run, which has none yet.

result.description:
The apply step's structured output and the run's usage total, once the
run has finished.

rows.description:
The reviewed rows: the executor's live buffer while running, the job
result after. Rows are deliberately **not** pushed through the generic
jobs feed.

schema.title: AgentRunDetail

post.description: Closes a run this caller owns with its terminal status.

schema.description:
The answer of a write that has nothing to report but that it
happened: `{"ok": true}`.

ok.description: Always `true`; a failure is an error answer instead.

schema.title: Ack

post.description: Appends one ledger event, an array of them, or an NDJSON batch to a run this caller owns, straight into the run's live buffer, which the dashboard's Run tab reads.

schema.description: Newline-delimited JSON: one value per line, each decoded as the application/json form's single-object case.
`POST /api/agents/runs/{job_id}/events` — what became of the batch.

applied.description: How many events went into the run.

ok.description: Always `true`: rejected events are reported below, not failed.

rejected.description:
One line per event the run did not take (unparseable, or refused by
the run's rules), in the order they were sent.

schema.title: AgentEventsApplied

get.description: One agent's full definition: the complete document for owner credentials or, for the agent's own token, the same document with host paths substituted out.

schema.description: `GET /api/agents/{id}` — everything the detail page's three tabs need.

batch.description:
The run surface a `batch` or `container` agent offers. `None` for a
`chat` agent.

budget.description: The two Responses settings a turn is bounded by, shown next to Apply.

config.description:
Stored config values with every `secret` field replaced by
`{ "has_value": bool }`. The value itself never leaves the process.

currency.description:
The gateway's display currency, so a run's cost is printed the way the
Usage page prints every other one.

dev_url.description:
The dev-server override. While it is set, `/agents/<id>/app/**`
goes there and no container is started for the app; runs and applies
still use the image. Empty means "served from the image".

error.description:
Set when the stored manifest could not be read at all — a row written by
a newer build. The document still comes back `200` with whatever could
be read, so the Definition editor stays reachable for the very manifest
that needs fixing; a `400` here would lock the client out of it.

fields.description: The config schema flattened into form fields, in document order.

last_run.description:
The agent's most recent run, with its outcome (`status`, `error`, tokens,
cost) — the same summary the catalog card carries. While a run is in
flight it is that run. Absent when the agent has never run, when
retention pruned its runs, and on a row this build cannot read.

live_job.description: The run in flight, if any.

manifest.description:
The manifest as stored: the canonical serialization, **as text** — what
the Definition editor loads and what Export writes.

Text and not a `serde_json::Value` on purpose. `serde_json::Map` is a
`BTreeMap`, so a `Value` here would alphabetize the config schema's
properties and silently re-sort the form the author laid out.
Parse it client-side if a tree is needed, and post it back to
`agent_set` as a **string**: an object argument is accepted but arrives
already re-sorted, and the import report says so.

portability.description:
Whether an export of this agent would land on another box, and what the
receiver would have to do if not. The same answer the export file's
`portability` key carries, on the page that offers the download.

provenance.description:
Where this row was installed from. `None` for a row that came
from a pasted manifest rather than from an image.

resettable.description: A shipped manifest exists for this id, so "Reset to shipped" applies.

runtime.description: What a `container` agent runs under. `None` for every other kind.

service.description:
Service mode, when the manifest declares it.
`None` means no App tab, no proxy route and no `agent:<id>` MCP row.

token.description:
The agent's own token — its name, whether one has been minted, and the scope it
currently carries. **Never the value**:
that comes from `agent_token_get`, which is what Copy token calls.

warnings.description:
Warnings that are not tool gaps. Start is disabled while any of them carries
`blocks_start`.

schema.title: AgentDetail

get.description: Downloads the agent as `<id>.agent.json`: its manifest plus an envelope (export time, lmgw version, portability, the names of the secret and folder fields left out, and — with include_config=1 — the non-secret config values). A secret never leaves; the file imports back unchanged.

schema.description: `1` adds the **non-secret** config values as `config_values`.

`GET /api/agents/{id}/export` — the `<id>.agent.json` file: the agent's
manifest with an envelope around it. The manifest's fields sit at the top
level of the file, in the order the manifest has them; the envelope's own
fields follow.

config_omitted.description:
The `secret` config fields left out, so the receiver knows what to
fill in. Absent when there are none.

config_unbound.description:
The folder and file slots left out: they are paths on the exporting
machine, so the receiver chooses its own. Absent when there are none.

config_values.description: The non-secret config values; only with `include_config=1`.

lmgw_version.description: The lmgw version that wrote the file.

portability.description:
Whether the file runs on another machine as it is, and what the
receiver would have to do if not.

schema.title: AgentExport

get.description: This agent's run history. For the agent's own token, a run's error text has host paths substituted out the same way the detail read does.

post.description: Opens a run from outside lmgw, exactly as the manifest's own trigger would. An agent has at most one live run: a second open while one is live is refused with the running job's id.

schema.description: `POST /api/agents/{id}/runs` — a run opened from outside lmgw.

deadline_seconds.description: How long the run has before lmgw ends it; `0` is no deadline.

run.description:
The run's job id, for `/api/agents/runs/{job_id}` and its events and
close routes.

schema.title: AgentRunOpened

schema.description:
`POST /api/agents/{id}/runs` refused with `409`: the agent already has a
run in flight, and `run` is its job id, so the caller can watch that one.

run.description: The job id of the run that is in flight.

schema.title: AgentRunConflict

409.description: Error, with this body rather than the default one.

get.description: audio.cpp's own spec catalog, from the cached snapshot only — an absent fetched_at means "never fetched here"; a page load never waits on GitHub.

schema.description:
`GET /api/audio/catalog` — the *cached* spec catalog. Never fetches: the
snapshot comes from memory or the kv store, and `POST /api/op/audio_catalog`
(`action: "refresh"`) is the only thing that goes to the network.

families.description: Families with an installed package or a served model come first.

fetched_at.description: RFC3339 fetch time of the snapshot; absent when nothing is cached yet.

warnings.description:
What the last refresh could not do — a spec file that did not load, a
package repo Hugging Face could not list (offline, rate-limited,
gated) — or that it has not checked the package files yet. Stays until
the next refresh. Absent when there are none.

schema.title: AudioCatalog

get.description: Every reachable base URL, whether a key is required, the models a client can already see, and the expose-all upstream prefixes — the connect panel a fresh client reads to configure itself.

schema.description: `GET /api/connect` — how to reach the gateway and what it exposes.

bases.description:
Every URL that reaches the gateway (wildcard binds expand to
loopback + LAN addresses).

catalog_prefixes.description:
Prefixes of enabled `expose_all` upstreams whose catalogs pass
through dynamically (rendered as ghost entries, not copyable names).

device_port.description:
The device listener's port (`devices.port`, else the HTTP port plus
one): what "this computer" pairs on, `https://127.0.0.1:<port>`.
`null` when none can be derived (device link design §3.1).

device_urls.description:
The URLs the pairing form proposes for another device (device link
design §3.1, §3.2): the addresses a device can count on, the stable
LAN and WireGuard ones first, each with its interface. Empty when
the machine has none, or no port can be derived.

schema.title: ConnectInfo

schema.title: ChunksResponse

schema.description:
`GET /api/docs/corpora` — the Docs tab's list, its badges, and the two
gateway-level facts it needs alongside them.

rerank_model.description: Alias the rerank stage would call; `null` when there is none.

schema.title: DocsOverview

post.description: Creates a corpus, resolving and pinning its embed and ingest models before the row exists. start: true queues the ingest job immediately.

embed_model.description:
Model alias to embed with. Probed now, and the *resolved* identity is
what the corpus pins.

ingest_model.description:
Model alias that will drive extraction. Validated now so the wizard
fails at the form rather than in the job.

schema.description:
`POST /api/docs/corpora` — the corpus that now exists, and the ingest job
when it was asked to start one.

job_id.description:
The ingest job queued with the corpus; `null` when `start` was not
asked for (the corpus is then empty until an ingest is started).

ok.description: Always `true`; a refusal is an error answer instead.

schema.title: CorpusCreated

schema.description: `GET /api/docs/corpora/{id}`.
schema.title: CorpusDetail

post.description: Deletes a corpus and everything ingested into it. 404 not_found for a corpus id nothing has.

schema.description: A write that reports what it did in a sentence: `{"ok": true, "message": …}`.

message.description: What was done, for a person to read.

ok.description: Always `true`; a failure is an error answer instead.

schema.description:
What the ingest / re-embed / eval / golden-generate triggers answer: the job
that is now running, or the one that already was.

`true` when a job of that kind for the corpus was already in flight:

params.description:
Stage overrides to measure under; absent measures under the defaults
`docs__query` itself runs with.

schema.description:
What the ingest / re-embed / eval / golden-generate triggers answer: the job
that is now running, or the one that already was.

`true` when a job of that kind for the corpus was already in flight:

post.description: Creates or edits (id present) a golden query. Expected chunk ids are validated against the corpus before they are stored. 404 not_found for a corpus id nothing has.

id.description: Present = edit that query; absent = create one.

origin.description:
`manual` (default) or `synthetic` — a curated candidate keeps saying
where it came from.

A golden query written: `POST /api/docs/golden` and accepting a

`GET /api/docs/golden/candidates?corpus_id=[&status=]` — the curation
queue. `chunks` carries the sections the candidates were written from, keyed

The expectation as edited before accepting; absent keeps the chunk the
candidate was written from.

query.description: The query as edited before accepting; absent accepts it as proposed.

A golden query written: `POST /api/docs/golden` and accepting a

The answer of a write that has nothing to report but that it

per_chunk.description: Questions to ask for per sampled chunk. Absent means one.

sample.description:
Chunks to sample. Absent or `0` samples every chunk in the corpus — the
run is as big as the corpus unless a smaller sample is asked for.

schema.description:
What the ingest / re-embed / eval / golden-generate triggers answer: the job
that is now running, or the one that already was.

get.description: The live feed the dashboard opens once and keeps: stats, jobs, runtime, vram, mcp, updates and chat frames on connect, then request/stats/mcp/jobs/vram/runtime/updates frames as they change, a keys frame when a key's state moves without a request (a device's connection opened or closed, a key disabled, rotated or deleted), and a chat frame naming the threads, folders and messages any writer changed in the Chat (a device, an owner key, this or another dashboard window, the sweep): read them again. The first change of a burst waits a fixed 200 ms for the rest, then one read names everything changed up to it, so a stream sends at most one chat frame per 200 ms plus that read (but for one its keep-alive read finds). The chat frame on connect is a resync: read everything shown again, since frames are not replayed across a reconnect. Never closes on its own.

chat.description:
Something in the Chat changed: the `chat` frame of `/api/events`. The
frame names what changed and the dashboard reads it again; it carries no
rendering of its own.

It covers every writer: the dashboard (this window or another), a paired
device, an owner key, the self-admin tools and the gateway's own sweep.
`/api/events` is the owner's, so every thread is named, Admin Chat
included. Temporary chats are never named: they live in the memory of
the gateway, outside the change feed.

- **On connect** the stream sends one with `resync: true`: what a client
  read before it connected may be stale, so it reads everything it shows
  again. A reconnect is a connect, so frames missed while the stream was
  down are covered by that one.
- **Bursts are coalesced**: the first change of a burst waits a fixed
  200 ms (not a setting) for the rest, then the stream reads what changed
  once and sends one frame naming everything changed up to that read. A
  frame therefore comes 200 ms plus one read of the change feed after the
  first change it names, and a stream sends at most one frame per 200 ms,
  except one its keep-alive read finds (`chat_feed_keepalive_s`, a write
  that did not wake the feed). An id is named once however often it
  changed in a frame. A client that reads frames more slowly than they
  come may merge them (`merge`): a frame is a delta, never a
  state.

folders.description:
The folders created, changed (name, defaults, ongoing, retention) or
deleted, and those whose current thread moved, ascending.

messages.description:
The threads whose messages changed, ascending: a message added (a
user turn, typed or spoken, as it is stored; a reply as it is saved),
edited, continued, cut to what was heard, or deleted. A reply still
being generated is not named until it is saved.

resync.description:
What changed is not known: read everything shown again. Sent on
connect, and when the stream could not tell what changed.

threads.description:
The threads whose row changed, ascending: created (a rollover's new
current thread too), renamed, settings, pinned, archived or
restored, moved between folders, hidden from devices, or deleted.

keys.description:
A key's state moved without a request landing: the `keys` frame of
`/api/events`. A device's connection opened or closed — its online state
and `last_seen_at` — or a key was disabled, rotated or deleted. The Keys
page refetches its list on it, instead of polling.

`link` (a device's connection opened or closed), `disabled`,
`rotated` or `deleted`; a device's pairing (device link design §9.3):
`token` (a pairing token minted or ended), `enrolled` (a device sent
its key: the row's code and peer address are in its `pairing`),
`confirmed`, `contested` (a used token came back with another key);
or `resync` (with `key_id` 0) when the event stream could not deliver
every frame: refetch the keys.

Name of the gateway API key that made the call (never the key itself);

capability: "fallback 'x' lacks vision: 3 images sent as
placeholders", "'m' lacks audio: transcript sent", several joined by
"; ". `None` = nothing was degraded.

(the GPU hold), `external_vram` (VRAM outside lmgw's control was

(a candidate alias with no model it may use). `None` = no

post.description: multipart/form-data, one part per file (the part's file name is the stored name, reduced to its last path component). The whole request is bounded by the max_body_mb setting (0 is unbounded): 413 body_limit naming it, for a declared or a streamed body. Each file's kind is sniffed from its bytes, never its name: images and audio are refused, as is an empty file. The answer has one item per part: `added`, `replaced` (the name existed with other bytes, or its ingest had failed; the file is queued again), `unchanged` (same name, same bytes), `duplicate` (same bytes under another name) or `refused` with the `reason`. A refused file does not fail the request. Added and replaced files are queued and the ingest job is started or joined: `job` is its id (`null` when nothing was queued). Ingestion — reading, chunking, embedding, a vision model for text-less PDF pages — runs in that job; observe it as for Resume. 400 no_files for a request without any part, 400 bad_request for a malformed multipart body.

post.description: Starts the one job the base needs, or joins the one already running: a re-embed (`kb_reembed`) when chunks lack a vector or the base is marked `re_embed_required`, otherwise an ingest (`kb_ingest`) of the pending files. The route only starts the job and answers at once with its id in `job`; measuring the stored chunks against the model, re-chunking what does not fit and embedding all run in the job. When the last re-embed was refused as larger than the model's input, the files holding the oversized chunks are marked pending and an ingest (`kb_ingest`) re-chunks them instead: `kind` is `kb_ingest`, and `rechunk` says why. A base with nothing waiting answers `job: null` and a message. Observe progress with the job: `GET /api/jobs` lists it (key `kb:{id}`), the `jobs` frames of `GET /api/events` stream it, and the base's own `job` field keeps the last outcome. A file that failed is not retried here; re-ingest it.

A model or chunk-size change while a job runs on the base is refused (400 op_failed naming the job): wait for it or cancel it first. Other refusals as for create.

default_request_options.description: Request-option defaults applied to every call, as a JSON object (a JSON string here), e.g. '{"speed": 1.1}' — the family's 'request' options. A request that names one still wins.

default_voice_preset.description: The voice a request that names none gets: a preset name from voice_presets, or an inline preset as a JSON object string. Empty clears.

enabled.description: Serve this model (a disabled model has no container).

extra_run_args.description: 'podman run' args override, one argument per entry. Absent leaves it unchanged; name it in 'clear' to revert to the class default — which carries the GPU and SELinux flags, so override it only knowingly. An override with no args is never stored: it is the class default. A row on the CPU runs its own override as written; one that still passes a GPU is named in lmgw__local_model_get's problems.

family.description: audio.cpp model family, e.g. 'pocket_tts' or 'qwen3_asr' — the catalog's family id. Required on create.

hold_fallback.description: Model alias to route to while GPU hold is active, when hold_fallback_mode is 'alias' — a cloud audio model. Unused on a row on the CPU, which the hold does not stop.

hold_fallback_mode.description: Where a request against this model goes while GPU hold is active. 'inherit' (default) means NO fallback for this class; 'alias' routes to hold_fallback instead.

image.description: Podman image override for this model's own container. Empty clears back to the audio class image.

lazy.description: Load the model on its first request (true) or at container start (false). Omit to inherit the audio class setting; name 'lazy' in clear to go back to inheriting.

load_options.description: audio.cpp load options as a JSON object (written as a JSON string on this tool plane), e.g. '{"language": "de"}' — the family's 'load' options. Replaces the stored object; '{}' empties it.

mode.description: 'offline' (default: one buffered answer) or 'streaming' (the family streams its output as server-sent events).

model_id.description: Client-facing model id (the part after the audio prefix, so 'audio/<model_id>'). Required on create. Without id it selects the row to update, delete, enable or disable; WITH id, on update, it renames the row, and the old container is removed.

model_spec_override.description: A '<family>.json' spec (or a directory of them) relative to the audio models dir that replaces the image's built-in catalog for this row. Empty clears.

path.description: The model directory, RELATIVE to the audio models dir — a package's suggested_path, e.g. 'audio-cpp/audio.cpp-gguf/PocketTTS-GGUF/german'. Required on create.

session_options.description: audio.cpp session options as a JSON object (a JSON string here), e.g. '{"weight_type": "q8_0"}' — the family's 'session' options. Replaces the stored object; '{}' empties it.

task.description: What the model does: tts, asr, gen (music, sound), clon (voice cloning), vc, svc, s2s, sep (separation), vad, diar, align, vdes (voice design), spk, midi. A package's suggested_task. Required on create.

Name 'threads' in clear for the default: this machine's physical cores for a row switched to the CPU (backend='cpu' on the row), the audio class's threads for every other row — one that inherits a class backend of cpu included. Several CPU rows busy at once each run their own pool, so split the cores between them.

voice_presets.description: Named voices as a JSON object (a JSON string here): name -> {"voice_id": "<shipped voice>"} or {"voice_ref": "/models/<clip>.wav"}, e.g. '{"alba": {"voice_id": "alba"}}'. Replaces the stored object.

post.description: Create, update, delete, enable or disable an AUX model: an embedding model (served on /v1/embeddings with --embeddings), a reranker (served on /v1/rerank with --reranking) or a decision model (a GGUF whose header declares decision.type, served on /v1/systemone). This is the class for models that answer without generating: encoders, whose header declares a pooling_type or a classifier head and which have no LM head, and decision models, causal ones included, which llama-server serves without a generation route. Neither can be a chat model. Aux models live in their own models directory (download with lmgw__hf_add target=aux, list with lmgw__gguf_files target=aux) and are exposed under their kind's prefix, both in lmgw__settings' aux_router: public_prefix for embedders and rerankers (usually 'embed/<model_id>'), decision_prefix for decision models (usually 'decide/<model_id>'); a row answers to its own prefix only. Get kind, pooling and ctx_size (and for a decision model ubatch_size, batch_size and backend) from lmgw__local_model_plan target=aux rather than guessing: the wrong pooling produces vectors that look fine and retrieve garbage. Update is partial: pass only what changes, and use 'clear' to unset a field. A model's own container starts on its first request; lmgw__local_model_test target=aux then proves it embeds, reranks or answers one System One question.

schema.description:
Sparse patch for an aux (embedding / rerank / decision) model — a slimmer
sibling of the local model patch: no sampling, no template, no
speculation. What an aux row *does* need beyond a path is its kind and,
for embedders, the pooling the model was trained with; both are read out
of the GGUF by `lmgw__local_model_plan target=aux`.

Placement, the batch sizes and a projector are fields
(decision-models design §3.3): `backend`, `threads`, `ubatch_size`,
`batch_size`, `mmproj_path`.

backend.description: 'cpu' runs the model on the CPU: --n-gpu-layers 0, the class's run args without the GPU passthrough, no VRAM charged, and it keeps serving while the GPU hold is on. Omit to keep the current value; an empty string (or 'backend' in clear) runs it on the GPU.

batch_size.description: --batch-size, 1 or more; omit for llama-server's default.

clear.description: Field names to reset to unset, comma-separated: 'extra_args', 'extra_run_args', 'image', 'hold_fallback' (resets both mode and alias), 'ctx_size', 'ubatch_size', 'batch_size', 'mmproj_path', 'backend', 'threads'.

ctx_size.description: Context length (--ctx-size). Use the model's trained context from the plan; llama-server refuses a longer input with an error rather than truncating it. 'ctx_size' in clear takes llama-server's default.

enabled.description: Serve this model (a disabled model has no container).

extra_args.description: Escape hatch for llama-server flags with no field above, one argument per entry (['--flash-attn', 'on']). --embeddings, --reranking, --pooling, --ctx-size, --ubatch-size, --batch-size, --mmproj, --n-gpu-layers and --threads are rendered from the fields above; a copy here is ignored when its field is set.

extra_run_args.description: 'podman run' args override, one argument per entry. Absent leaves it unchanged; name it in 'clear' to revert to the class default. An override with no args is never stored: it is the class default.

gguf_path.description: Weights GGUF, relative to the AUX models directory (e.g. 'Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B-GGUF/Qwen3-Embedding-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf'). Required on create. Files in the chat models directory cannot be addressed — download into the aux dir with lmgw__hf_add target=aux.

hold_fallback.description: Model alias to route to while GPU hold is active, when hold_fallback_mode is 'alias'. Must resolve to a non-local route.

hold_fallback_mode.description: Where a request against this model goes while GPU hold is active. 'inherit' (default) means NO fallback for this class — aux models never inherit the global chat fallback, because a different embedding model silently corrupts a vector index; 'alias' routes to hold_fallback instead.

idle_seconds.description: Seconds idle before the model unloads. 0 = never. Default 300.

image.description: Podman image override for this model's own container. Empty or absent leaves it unset; 'clear' reverts to the aux class image.

kind.description: 'embed' (default on create) serves /v1/embeddings; 'rerank' serves /v1/rerank; 'decision' serves /v1/systemone (no kind flag, no pooling). lmgw__model_inspect reports which a file is.

mmproj_path.description: A projector (--mmproj) relative to the AUX models directory, for a model that reads images (a vision-language embedder, an image-capable decision model). Use the one lmgw__local_model_plan finds beside the weights. Charged with the weights. Empty string clears.

model_id.description: Client-facing model id (the part after the aux prefix); also selects the row when id is omitted.

pooling.description: Pooling strategy (--pooling) for an embedding model. Use the value lmgw__local_model_plan reads from the GGUF header; omit to let llama-server pick the model's default. Never set on a rerank model (--reranking selects rank pooling itself, and a second pooling flag breaks it) or a decision model. Empty string clears.

threads.description: --threads, 1 or more. Unset renders none on the GPU, and on the CPU this machine's physical cores (the logical CPU count where the core topology cannot be read) unless extra_args name a count.

ubatch_size.description: --ubatch-size, 1 or more; omit for llama-server's default. An encoder whose input llama-server cannot split (any but a last-token embedder or a causal reranker) evaluates its whole input in one ubatch, so this bounds every input it answers; lmgw__local_model_plan sets it to the context there. Raise batch_size with it: llama.cpp lowers the ubatch to the batch. The VRAM ledger charges the compute buffer it grows.

A run of a large model at a long context takes minutes; its top points come from the model's real context, nothing is capped. Returns run_id and job_id at once: follow it with lmgw__bench_run id=<run_id>; lmgw__bench_cancel ends it early (partial results are kept). post.description: Container builds: lmgw can build its own llama.cpp / ik_llama.cpp / audio.cpp / stable-diffusion.cpp server images from git — a repository and ref, plus PRs or other branches merged on top — and tags each result 'localhost/lmgw-<engine-repo>:<slug>' (the MOVING tag, which follows the build's last verified run) and '…:<slug>-<base7>-<cfg6>' (immutable, one per run). Without id: every build with its newest run (last_run), the run its moving tag points at (current_run), the job id of a run in progress (live_job_id, null when idle) and who uses its moving tag (used_by: class defaults, model overrides, containers running or stopped) and its 'update' badge: null before the first update check (every build_update_check_hours; see lmgw__settings) or when it has no succeeded run to compare with, else {checked_at, reasons, ref_moved, extras, errors} — reasons like 'master +37 commits', 'master moved (abc1234 → def5678)', 'PR #1234 pushed', 'PR #1234 merged upstream and contained in your base — drop it' (only once the build's own base is proven to already hold the PR's merge or head commit; otherwise 'PR #1234 merged upstream at <date>; your base doesn't contain it yet — it's still merged into your build'), 'PR #1234 closed unmerged', 'definition changed since last run (ref)'; empty reasons = up to date as of checked_at; what could not be checked (a forge rate limit with its reset time) is in errors. An update is acted on with lmgw__build_run. Also 'repo_presets' — the repository presets (the id is what lmgw__build_set preset= takes). With id: that build and its runs, newest first, each with its status (running; succeeded; unverified = built but not GPU-checked, e.g. under the GPU hold; broken = a verify check failed; failed; canceled; up_to_date = those exact inputs were already built and verified), resolved commits, image, tags, size, verify result and error. Poll this with id after lmgw__build_run until live_job_id is null.

post.description: The answer follows the action: `preview` answers CandidateAliasPreview (the draft's derivation and the models it could add, written nowhere), every other action CandidateAliasSaved.

schema.description:
Sparse patch for a candidate alias. Every list-shaped field is flat text
(no nested objects, no arrays), comma/space/newline separated like `extra_run_args`.

action.description: What to do. 'preview' validates and derives a draft (any of the fields below, over an existing row named by id/alias or a brand-new one) without saving it — the same response shape, plus 'addable' (local chat models not yet in candidates and which enabled facet each would drop) and an 'error' that never aborts the rest of the answer.

alias.description: The client-facing model name. On create this is the new alias; otherwise it selects the row (pass id as well to rename). Refused if it already names a plain alias or a local model of any class.

background.description: Scheduled/background traffic: never evicts a model foreground requests use, never waits, and may only start the primary into free VRAM or evict another idle background-owned entry. Default false.

candidates.description: Local chat model ids (lmgw__local_model_set rows, not aliases), one per line or comma-separated. The FIRST is the primary — the only one the alias ever starts; the rest are alternates in preference order, used only when already loaded. Every id must name an enabled local chat model. On update, absent leaves the stored list unchanged; it can never be saved empty — delete the alias instead.

capabilities_disabled.description: Facet names switched OFF, one per line or comma-separated: vision, audio, tool_calls, reasoning, structured_output. This is the FULL desired list of the alias's own switches, not a delta and never auto-filled — every facet not named here that every candidate currently supports ends up enabled, including one that becomes supported later (it turns on by itself unless named here). On create, nothing is refused: an unsupported facet is simply left off. On update, switching a facet back on (removing it from this list) or leaving an already-enabled facet unnamed while a candidate drops it is refused, naming the facet. Absent leaves the stored list unchanged; use clear=capabilities_disabled to reset it to empty (every common facet back on).

clear.description: Field names to reset to unset, comma-separated: capabilities_disabled, notes.

fallback.description: The alias this candidate alias falls back to when fallback_mode is 'alias'. Must resolve, must not itself be local, and must not be another candidate alias.

fallback_mode.description: How this alias' one fallback resolves. 'inherit' reads the global GPU-hold fallback; 'none' refuses (503 gpu_hold / gpu_deferred) rather than leave the machine; 'alias' routes to 'fallback'. Default inherit.

schema.title: CandidateAliasPatch

schema.description:
What `candidate_alias_set` answers, by `action`: `CandidateAliasPreview`
for `preview`, `CandidateAliasSaved` for every other.

The two shapes share most keys, so this is the document's description of
the one op, not a type to read an answer into: a reader knows the action it
sent and reads that action's type.
schema.title: CandidateAliasAnswer

post.description: Control the per-model container runtime: lmgw runs one podman container per loaded chat/aux/audio/image model, started on demand and stopped independently — there is no shared per-class container any more. Address one model with `model=<id>` (its class is found automatically from the local/aux/audio/image tables; pass `target` too only to disambiguate an id that exists in more than one class); address a whole group with `target` alone. 'start' on a model warms it (a no-op if it is already up); 'start' on a group only starts that group's warm_start-flagged models, never every configured one — starting an entire class at once can ask for more VRAM than the box has, so start any other model on demand with `model=<id>`. 'stop' refuses a model still serving requests unless `override=true`. 'restart' and 'apply' are the same operation on a single model (stop, then start with freshly rendered arguments — there is no drift concept, argv is always rendered fresh); on a group, 'apply' additionally reports the same pre-flight lmgw__local_model_check runs (missing files, spec_type mismatches) for every enabled model in scope, not only the running ones. 'logs' (model only) returns the container's recent output — with one container per model this is the only place a failed start is visible. 'status' shows, for a llama-server container, what it said about itself in GET /props at its start (llama_props: build_info, modalities, n_ctx_slot — null where the server did not say), or among its warnings why it could not.

model.description: Address one model by its id instead of a whole group.

override.description: Force a 'stop' that would otherwise be refused because the model is still serving requests.

tail.description: Lines of container output 'logs' returns, from the end. Default 60.

target.description: Which group of models. Omit when 'model' is given.

schema.description:
Which shape an answer has follows from the address and the action; every
shape carries `ok`. The actions that change something add a `message`, a
`note` or both (apply); the status and log answers carry neither.
schema.title: ContainerAnswer

post.description: Replace lmgw's device CA: a new key under a new wrapping key and a new certificate replace tls/ca.key and tls/ca.crt, and the old key is not kept. Every enrolled device loses its key and certificate (its policy kept) and must be paired again with a new token; what each holds open closes at once, and every pairing token alive ends, since its link pins the old CA. The server certificates are issued anew. Answers DeviceCaRotated with the new fp and the devices reset.

schema.description:
`POST /api/op/device_ca_rotate`: lmgw's device CA replaced (device link
design §5.5); every enrolled device was reset to wait for a new token.

devices_reset.description:
The devices reset, by name without `device:`: each lost its key and
its certificate and waits for **New token…**.

fp.description:
The new CA's pin: `sha256:` and the hex SHA-256 of its
SubjectPublicKeyInfo, what every new pairing link carries.

message.description: What was done, for a person to read.

ok.description: Always `true`; a refusal is an error answer instead.

schema.title: DeviceCaRotated

post.description: Confirm the key a device enrolled, after comparing the code the Keys list shows (pairing.confirm_code) with the one the device shows, and sending that code: the key waiting for the confirmation must have it, else 409 confirm_code_mismatch and nothing changes (a card showing an earlier enrolment confirms nothing). Until then every request of that key is refused 403 device_unconfirmed; from now on it is served. A key that waited beside one the device kept (a re-pair that kept the current key) replaces it: the kept key ends, and what it holds open closes. Answers DeviceConfirmed with the code confirmed and whether it replaced a kept key.

confirm_code.description: The code the device shows, compared with the Keys list's pairing.confirm_code: eight hex digits, e.g. 7F3A-91C2 (either case; the hyphen and spaces optional). The key waiting for the confirmation must have it, or nothing is confirmed (409 confirm_code_mismatch).

id.description: Device id, from the Keys table.

schema.description:
`POST /api/op/device_confirm`: the owner confirmed a device's enrolment
(device link design §3.5); its next request is served.

confirm_code.description:
The confirmation code of the key confirmed, `7F3A-91C2`: the one the
device shows, and the one the call sent.

message.description: What was done, for a person to read.

name.description: `device:<name>`.

ok.description: Always `true`; a refusal is an error answer instead.

replaced.description:
Whether the confirmed key replaced one the device kept until now (a
re-pair that kept the current key, §5.2): the kept key ended, and
what it held open closed.

schema.title: DeviceConfirmed

post.description: A new one-time pairing token for a device row, replacing its earlier one; the row keeps its id, policy and history. end_current: true ends the key the device holds now (a lost or stolen device): what it holds open closes at once, as on a disable, and its requests are refused until the new token enrols. Left out or false, the current key works on: a new key the token enrols waits beside it for its own confirmation (device_confirm), which ends the current key (a new phone), and the same key enrolling again gets a fresh certificate and keeps its confirmation (a renewal before the old one lapses). A key that waited from an earlier token, and the contested mark, go with the new token. local_only and urls replace the row's, which a device paired before TLS has none of. Answers DevicePaired with the new link, as key_create does. Refused 409 device_listener_off while the device listener does not serve.

end_current.description: End the device's current key now: its connections close and its requests are refused until the new token enrols (a lost or stolen device). Default false: the current key works until the new token's enrolment replaces it.

id.description: Device id, from the Keys table.

local_only.description: Replace the device's "this computer" flag; default: as it is.

urls.description: Device keys: the device's lmgw URLs, https base URLs of the device listener in the order the device tries them (a LAN or WireGuard address, or a name; IP addresses and names of letters, digits and hyphens, which every server certificate carries). Default: for this computer https://127.0.0.1:<device port>; for another device every network address of this machine on the device port.

schema.description:
A device's pairing link minted: `POST /api/op/key_create` with `kind:
device` (the row and its first pairing token) and `device_token` (a new
token for the same row; device link design §3.2, §5.2). The token goes to
the owner once, inside the link.

fp.description:
`sha256:` and the hex SHA-256 of the device CA's SubjectPublicKeyInfo:
the link's `fp`, which the device's enrolment pins.

id.description: The device row's `api_keys.id`; a new token keeps it.

link.description:
`lmgw-pair:?v=2&name=…&url=…[&url=…]&fp=sha256:…&token=lmgw-enrol-…`:
carries the one-time pairing token to the device. Secret while its
token lives: shown once, never logged.

local_only.description:
Paired as "this computer": the device reaches lmgw on a loopback
address only.

message.description:
What was done, for a person to read: what the device does next, and
whether the device listener reaches it from where it is.

name.description: `device:<name>`.

ok.description: Always `true`; a refusal is an error answer instead.

token_expires_at.description:
When the pairing token lapses (RFC 3339, UTC): `devices.token_minutes`
after it was minted.

urls.description:
The device's lmgw URLs: `https` base URLs of the device listener, in
the owner's order, as the link carries them and enrolment answers
them.

post.description: Download a model from Hugging Face into the models directory — the normal way to get a new model onto this gateway. Fetches the weights file you name (or pick by quantization) together with its multimodal projector and, for target=chat, its speculative drafter from the same directory, because a model usually needs all of them. Split GGUFs expand to every part automatically. Downloads run in the background: poll lmgw__hf_downloads, then call lmgw__local_model_plan on the result. target=image downloads the stable-diffusion.cpp kinds (.safetensors, .ckpt, .pt, .pth as well as .gguf) into the image models dir and fetches no companions — an image pipeline's VAE and text encoders live in OTHER repos, so use lmgw__image_recipe_add to bring a whole family down in one call and this tool only for a single file a recipe does not cover.

companions.description: Also fetch the projector beside the weights, and for target=chat the drafter (an aux row has none). Default true; set false to download only the file you named.

file.description: Exact path of the weights file within the repo. Omit to select by quant instead.

quant.description: Pick the weights file by quantization label instead of exact name, e.g. 'Q4_K_XL' or 'IQ4_XS'. See lmgw__hf_repo for what is offered.

repo.description: Repo id like 'unsloth/Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF' — owner/name only, not a full huggingface.co URL.

target.description: Which models directory to download into. Default 'chat'. Use 'aux' for embedding, rerank and decision models and 'image' for stable-diffusion.cpp pipeline files — a row can only address files in its own class's directory, and this is what keeps the file in the updater's view (lmgw__hf_set check_updates).

`repo/`: the directory under the models dir that the repo's files land
in, with the trailing slash.

The tracked rows of the file asked for, the companions and every part

How many files went into the queue: the weights, the companions, and
every part of a split GGUF.

The class whose models dir the files go to: `chat | aux | audio |

What to look out for in what was queued, one sentence each; empty when
nothing. Today: a shard of a sharded `.safetensors` is queued alone,
and stable-diffusion.cpp cannot reassemble shards.

The answer follows the action: `check_updates` answers HfUpdatesChecked (how many finished downloads of the `target` class differ from the hub, and one sentence per file it could not ask about, in which case `ok` is false); `redownload`, `cancel` and `delete` answer a MessageAck.
